akhfash:11-11.t:
And He said ﴿مَّن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يُقْرِضُ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً﴾: this is not like borrowing out of need; rather, it is like the Arabs' saying: "لي عندَكَ قَرْضُ صِدُقٍ" (I have a good loan with you) and "قَرْضُ سَوءٍ" (a bad loan), when one has done good or evil to another. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 269]:
سَأَجْزِي سَلاَمانَ بنَ مُفْرِجَ قَرْضَهُم * بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهُمْ وأَزَّلَتِ
(I will repay Salāmān ibn Mufrij their loan, for what their hands sent forth and bestowed.)

akhfash:12-12.t: He said ﴿يَسْعَىٰ نُورُهُم بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِم﴾: He means "on their right" — and Allah knows best — as He said ﴿يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ﴾, meaning "with a glance".

akhfash:13-13.t:
And He said ﴿ٱنظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِسْ مِن نُّورِكُمْ﴾ because it is from "نَظرْتُه", meaning "نَظرْتُ", "أَنَا أنْظُرُهُ", and its meaning is: I wait for him.
And He said ﴿بِسُورٍ لَّهُ بَابٌ﴾: its meaning is "and a wall was set up between them".

akhfash:22-22.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّبْرَأَهَآ﴾: He means — and Allah knows best — "except that it is in a Book", so implication was permitted in it. You may say: "عِنْدِي هذا لَيسَ إِلاَّ" (I have this, nothing but), meaning: "it is nothing but it".

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبُخْلِ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِيُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ﴾: He was satisfied with the statements in the Quran, as He said ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ﴾, and in this place there was no khabar (predicate). Allah knows best what He sends down; it is as He sent it down and as He willed it to be.

akhfash:29-29.t: And He said ﴿لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ أَلاَّ يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَيْءٍ﴾: He means "so that they may know".

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ that is, everything declares His transcendence; so the lām is added (mazīda); and مَا is used rather than مَنْ, giving precedence (taghlīb) to the majority; ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي﴾ by bringing into being ﴿وَيُمِيتُ﴾ after it; ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ﴾ before everything, without beginning, ﴿وَالْآخِرُ﴾ after everything, without end, ﴿وَالظَّاهِرُ﴾ through the proofs pointing to Him, ﴿وَالْبَاطِنُ﴾ hidden from the perception of the senses; ﴿وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ of the days of this world, the first of them Sunday and the last Friday; ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ the Kursī (Seat), an establishing befitting Him; ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ﴾ enters ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ such as rain and the dead, ﴿وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا﴾ such as plants and minerals, ﴿وَمَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾ such as mercy and punishment, ﴿وَمَا يَعْرُجُ﴾ ascends ﴿فِيهَا﴾ such as good and evil deeds; ﴿وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ﴾ by His knowledge ﴿أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ﴾ all existing things.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ﴾ He makes it enter ﴿فِي النَّهَارِ﴾ so that [the day] increases and the night decreases, ﴿وَيُولِجُ النَّهَارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ so that [the night] increases and the day decreases; ﴿وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in them of secrets and beliefs.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿آمِنُوا﴾ persevere in faith ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ in the way of Allah ﴿مِمَّا جَعَلَكُمْ مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ﴾ of the wealth of those who preceded you, and those after you will succeed you in it. It was revealed concerning the expedition of hardship (ghazwat al-ʿusra), which is the expedition of Tabūk. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْفَقُوا﴾ an allusion to ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him; ﴿لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لَا تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an address to the disbelievers, that is, there is nothing preventing you from believing ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ وَقَدْ أُخِذَ﴾ with ḍamma on the hamza and kasra on the khāʾ, and with fatḥa on both and the accusative of what follows them [أَخَذَ مِيثَاقَكُمْ], ﴿مِيثَاقُكُمْ﴾ upon it, that is, Allah took it in the world of the seeds (ʿālam al-dharr), when He made them testify about themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ that is, wishing to believe in Him, then hasten to it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ the verses of the Quran, ﴿لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ of disbelief ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ of faith; ﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ﴾ in bringing you out of disbelief into faith ﴿لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ﴾ after your faith, ﴿أَلَّا﴾ in it the nūn of أَنْ is assimilated into the lām of لَا, ﴿تُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ with what is in them, so your wealth will reach Him without the reward of spending, unlike if you spend it, for then you are rewarded. ﴿لَا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ﴾ of Mecca ﴿وَقَاتَلَ أُولَئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَقَاتَلُوا وَكُلًّا﴾ of the two groups — and in one reading in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) — ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ Paradise; ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ and He will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ﴾ by spending his wealth in the way of Allah, ﴿قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ by spending it for Allah, ﴿فَيُضَاعِفَهُ﴾ — and in one reading [فَيُضَعِّفَهُ] with the doubled [ʿayn] — ﴿لَهُ﴾ from ten to more than seven hundred, as mentioned in al-Baqara; ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ along with the multiplying ﴿أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ joined with good pleasure and favourable regard.

celaleyn:12-12.t: Remember ﴿يَوْمَ تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ يَسْعَى نُورُهُمْ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ in front of them, ﴿وَ﴾ it is ﴿بِأَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ and it is said to them: ﴿بُشْرَاكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ﴾ that is, entering them, ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتُ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا انْظُرُونَا﴾ look at us — and in one reading with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the ẓāʾ: give us respite — ﴿نَقْتَبِسْ﴾ we take a firebrand and light ﴿مِنْ نُورِكُمْ قِيلَ﴾ to them, mocking them: ﴿ارْجِعُوا وَرَاءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُورًا﴾ So they go back, ﴿فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ and the believers ﴿بِسُورٍ﴾ — it is said: it is the wall of al-Aʿrāf — ﴿لَهُ بَابٌ بَاطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ﴾ on the side of the believers, ﴿وَظَاهِرُهُ﴾ on the side of the hypocrites, ﴿مِنْ قِبَلِهِ الْعَذَابُ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿يُنَادُونَهُمْ أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ﴾ in obedience? ﴿قَالُوا بَلَى وَلَكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ with hypocrisy ﴿وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ﴾ misfortunes for the believers ﴿وَارْتَبْتُمْ﴾ you doubted the religion of Islam, ﴿وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمَانِيُّ﴾ the cravings, ﴿حَتَّى جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ death, ﴿وَغَرَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ﴾ Satan.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ لَا يُؤْخَذُ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ ﴿مِنْكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ وَلَا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ هِيَ مَوْلَاكُمْ﴾ more fitting for you, ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ is it.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْنِ﴾ has it not come time ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ — it was revealed concerning the Companions when they joked excessively — ﴿أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَمَا نَزَّلَ﴾ with the doubled and the light [zāy] [نَزَلَ] ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ the Quran, ﴿وَلَا يَكُونُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تَخْشَعَ, ﴿كَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ they are the Jews and the Christians, ﴿فَطَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَمَدُ﴾ the time between them and their prophets, ﴿فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ did not soften to the remembrance of Allah; ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿اعْلَمُوا﴾ an address to the believers mentioned, ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا﴾ with plants; so He does likewise with your hearts, by returning them to humility. ﴿قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ﴾ that point to Our power, by this and other things, ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ﴾ from التَّصَدُّقِ (giving charity), the tāʾ being assimilated into the ṣād, that is, those who gave charity, ﴿وَالْمُصَّدِّقَاتِ﴾ the women who gave charity — and in one reading with the ṣād light in both, from التَّصْدِيقِ, [meaning] faith — ﴿وَأَقْرَضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ referring to both males and females by taghlīb (giving precedence to the masculine); the verb is conjoined to the noun in the ṣila (relative clause) of al-, because in it [the noun] stands in the place of the verb; and the mention of the loan with its description after the giving of charity is a qualification of it; ﴿يُضَاعَفُ﴾ — and in one reading [يُضَعَّفُ] with the doubled [ʿayn] — that is, their loan, ﴿لَهُمْ وَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيقُونَ﴾ those intensive in affirming the truth, ﴿وَالشُّهَدَاءُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ against the deniers among the nations; ﴿لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ which point to Our oneness, ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ the Fire.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ﴾ adornment ﴿وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ﴾ that is, being occupied with it; as for acts of obedience and what helps toward them, they are of the matters of the Hereafter; ﴿كَمَثَلِ﴾ that is, it — in its pleasing you and its fading away — is like the likeness of ﴿غَيْثٍ﴾ rain ﴿أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ the cultivators ﴿نَبَاتُهُ﴾ the growth arising from it, ﴿ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ﴾ dries up ﴿فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَامًا﴾ fragments that fade away with the winds; ﴿وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ﴾ for whoever preferred this world to it, ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانٌ﴾ for whoever did not prefer this world to it; ﴿وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ the enjoyment in it is not ﴿إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ﴾

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿سَابِقُوا إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا كَعَرْضِ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ if one of them were joined to the other; and الْعَرْضُ means breadth; ﴿أُعِدَّتْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ ذَلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿مَا أَصَابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ through drought ﴿وَلَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ such as illness and loss of a child ﴿إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ﴾ meaning the Preserved Tablet ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَهَا﴾ We create it; and the same is said of blessing; ﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لِكَيْلَا﴾ كَيْ puts the verb in the accusative, in the sense of أَنْ, that is, He, Exalted is He, informed of that so that you not ﴿تَأْسَوْا﴾ grieve ﴿عَلَى مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا تَفْرَحُوا﴾ with the joy of insolence, but rather [with] the joy of gratitude for the blessing, ﴿بِمَا آتَاكُمْ﴾ with the long vowel: He has given you; and with the short vowel: has come to you from Him; ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ﴾ arrogant on account of what he has been given, ﴿فَخُورٍ﴾ boasting of it over people,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ﴾ with what is obligatory on them ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ﴾ with it — for them is a severe threat; ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ﴾ from what is obligatory on him, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) — and in one reading it is dropped — ﴿الْغَنِيُّ﴾ independent of others, ﴿الْحَمِيدُ﴾ to His friends.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا﴾ the angels, to the prophets, ﴿بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ with decisive proofs, ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ in the sense of the books, ﴿وَالْمِيزَانَ﴾ justice, ﴿لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ﴾ We brought it out of the mines, ﴿فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ﴾ with it one fights, ﴿وَمَنَافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ﴾ with the knowledge of witnessing — conjoined (maʿṭūf) to لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ — ﴿مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ﴾ by supporting His religion with instruments of war of iron and other things, ﴿وَرُسُلَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ of يَنْصُرُهُ, that is, absent from them in this world. Ibn ʿAbbās said: they support Him and do not see Him. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾ He has no need of support, but it benefits the one who gives it.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ وَجَعَلْنَا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتَابَ﴾ meaning the four books — the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Furqān — for they are among the descendants of Abraham; ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مُهْتَدٍ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنَا عَلَى آثَارِهِمْ بِرُسُلِنَا وَقَفَّيْنَا بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ وَجَعَلْنَا فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً وَرَهْبَانِيَّةً﴾ it is renouncing women and taking to hermitages; ﴿ابْتَدَعُوهَا﴾ of their own accord; ﴿مَا كَتَبْنَاهَا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ We did not command it of them, ﴿إِلَّا﴾ (meaning: but) they did it ﴿ابْتِغَاءَ رِضْوَانِ﴾ the good pleasure of ﴿اللَّهِ فَمَا رَعَوْهَا حَقَّ رِعَايَتِهَا﴾ since many of them abandoned it, disbelieved in the religion of Jesus and entered the religion of their king; and many of them remained on the religion of Jesus and believed in our Prophet; ﴿فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ in him ﴿مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ in Jesus, ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ and Jesus; ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ﴾ two shares ﴿مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ for your belief in the two prophets, ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ نُورًا تَمْشُونَ بِهِ﴾ on the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ), ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ﴾ that is, He informed you of that so that ﴿أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ﴾ of the Torah, who did not believe in Muhammad ﷺ, may know ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the meaning is: that they ﴿لَا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ contrary to their claim that they are the beloved of Allah and the people of His good pleasure; ﴿وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ﴾ He gives it ﴿مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ so He gave the believers among them their reward twice, as mentioned before; ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ﴾ a past verb, and لله: both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates); the nominal clause is circumstantial.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿لَهُ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is muḍāf. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُحْيِي﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَيُمِيتُ﴾ conjoined to يحيي. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هو is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) قدير. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is circumstantial.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what follows it is conjoined to it. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) عليم. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السموات; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. ﴿فِي سِتَّةِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلق. ﴿أَيَّامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اسْتَوى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿يَلِجُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنْها﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها﴾ the two clauses are conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿أَيْنَ ما﴾ a jussive conditional noun, in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar of كان. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun (ism), and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to بصير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿لَهُ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مُلْكُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is muḍāf. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) ترجع. ﴿تُرْجَعُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿الْأُمُورُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يُولِجُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي النَّهارِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِذاتِ﴾ both attached to عليم. ﴿الصُّدُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿آمِنُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿جَعَلَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ﴾ its second object. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to what precedes them; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ a resumptive particle and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آمِنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَجْرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَبِيرٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of أجر; the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause الذين.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and ما is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَالرَّسُولُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَدْعُوكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is circumstantial. ﴿لِتُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يدعوكم. ﴿بِرَبِّكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَخَذَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿مِيثاقَكُمْ﴾ its object; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun (ism). ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ its khabar; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُنَزِّلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلى عَبْدِهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿آياتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of آيات; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. ﴿لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), and its object, the fāʿil being latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ينزل. ﴿مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ both also attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna and its noun (ism). ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ both attached to what follows them. ﴿لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and رؤوف رحيم are two khabars; the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and ما is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَلَّا تُنْفِقُوا﴾ an infinitival (maṣdarī) and accusative-governing particle, لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ما, because it contains the sense of the verb. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلِلَّهِ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿مِيراثُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and it is muḍāf. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْتَوِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مَنْ﴾ the fāʿil of يستوي; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْفَقَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْفَتْحِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقاتَلَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ أَعْظَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿دَرَجَةً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to درجة. ﴿أَنْفَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَقاتَلُوا﴾ conjoined to أنفقوا. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and كلا is a fronted first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَعَدَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ with kasra; as fāʿil the Quranic text has ﴿اللَّهُ﴾.] ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to خبير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿مَنْ ذَا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿الَّذِي﴾ the relative noun is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative. ﴿يُقْرِضُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿قَرْضاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿حَسَناً﴾ its ṣifa (adjective). ﴿فَيُضاعِفَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya). ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is conjoined by the fāʾ to a verb indicated by the preceding verb. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ both attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. ﴿أَجْرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ a ṣifa of أجر; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿تَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ conjoined to المؤمنين; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿يَسْعى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative. ﴿نُورُهُمْ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, and it is muḍāf. ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to أيديهم. ﴿بُشْراكُمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿جَنَّاتٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying) of an omitted saying. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of جنات. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to خالدين. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), with no grammatical position. ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ a ṣifa of الفوز; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يوم ترى. ﴿يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَالْمُنافِقاتُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿انْظُرُونا﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿نَقْتَبِسْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ نُورِكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿ارْجِعُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَراءَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿فَالْتَمِسُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿نُوراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَضُرِبَ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿بِسُورٍ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and سور is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿لَهُ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿بابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of سور. ﴿باطِنُهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿الرَّحْمَةُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of باطنه, and the clause باطنه فيه الرحمة is a ṣifa of باب. ﴿وَظاهِرُهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ قِبَلِهِ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿الْعَذابُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of ظاهره, and the clause وظاهره.. is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿يُنادُونَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَلَمْ نَكُنْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and لم نكن: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its noun (ism) latent (mustatir). ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of نكن; the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer. ﴿وَلكِنَّكُمْ﴾ lākinna and its noun; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the khabar of لكن. ﴿وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ، وَارْتَبْتُمْ﴾ the words are conjoined to what precedes them, and the i'rab is clear. ﴿وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمانِيُّ﴾ a past verb, its object and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and genitive. ﴿جاءَ أَمْرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, which is muḍāf. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَغَرَّكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْغَرُورُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and اليوم is an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُؤْخَذُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِدْيَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿وَلا مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿هِيَ مَوْلاكُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿وَبِئْسَ﴾ an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm). ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ its fāʿil.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْنِ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter from its end. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَنْ تَخْشَعَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن. ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ its fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the fāʿil of يأن. ﴿لِذِكْرِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ a relative noun conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿نَزَلَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلا﴾ negative. ﴿يَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and its noun (ism); the clause is conjoined to تخشع. ﴿كَالَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of يكونوا. ﴿أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ﴾ a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and its second object. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿فَطالَ﴾ conjoined to أوتوا. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَمَدُ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to كثير. ﴿فاسِقُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿اعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna, and its noun (ism) is the Name of Majesty. ﴿يُحْيِ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ its object; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿مَوْتِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿بَيَّنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْآياتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعل.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿وَالْمُصَّدِّقاتِ﴾ conjoined to المصدقين. ﴿وَأَقْرَضُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its object; the clause is conjoined to the sense of the verb in المصدقين. ﴿قَرْضاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿حَسَناً﴾ a ṣifa (adjective). ﴿يُضاعَفُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun standing in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿أَجْرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ a ṣifa; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a resumptive particle and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ conjoined to the Name of Majesty. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), with no grammatical position. ﴿الصِّدِّيقُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of أولئك; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين, and the clause الذين.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالشُّهَداءُ﴾ conjoined to الصديقون. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place, and it is muḍāf. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿أَجْرُهُمْ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَنُورُهُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the nominal clause is a second khabar of أولئك. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a resumptive particle and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾ conjoined to كفروا. ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both attached to كفروا. ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين, and the clause الذين is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿اعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّمَا﴾ the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ a ṣifa (adjective). ﴿لَعِبٌ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿وَلَهْوٌ﴾ conjoined to لعب. ﴿وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفاخُرٌ﴾ both also conjoined; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿وَتَكاثُرٌ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الْأَمْوالِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) تكاثر. ﴿وَالْأَوْلادِ﴾ conjoined to الأموال. ﴿كَمَثَلِ﴾ both attached to the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿غَيْثٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَباتُهُ﴾ a past verb, its object and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣifa of غيث. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَهِيجُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَتَراهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مُصْفَرًّا﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَكُونُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, its noun (ism) latent. ﴿حُطاماً﴾ its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿شَدِيدٌ﴾ a ṣifa; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ conjoined to عذاب. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to مغفرة. ﴿وَرِضْوانٌ﴾ conjoined to مغفرة. ﴿وَمَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ a ṣifa. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مَتاعُ﴾ khabar, and it is muḍāf. ﴿الْغُرُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿سابِقُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلى مَغْفِرَةٍ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ both attached to مغفرة; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجَنَّةٍ﴾ conjoined to مغفرة. ﴿عَرْضُها﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَعَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate), and it is muḍāf. ﴿السَّماءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السماء; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of جنة. ﴿أُعِدَّتْ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause is a second ṣifa of جنة. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَرُسُلِهِ﴾ conjoined to بالله. ﴿ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُؤْتِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ﴾ its second object. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause يؤتيه is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْفَضْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ a ṣifa of الفضل; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ﴾ a past verb, whose fāʿil (agent) is مصيبة, on the view that من is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to في الأرض. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فِي كِتابٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿أَنْ نَبْرَأَها﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the hāʾ is its object and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); أن and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِنَّ ذلِكَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to يسير. ﴿يَسِيرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿لِكَيْلا﴾ the lām is a preposition, كي is an infinitival (maṣdarī) and accusative-governing particle, and لا is negative. ﴿تَأْسَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from كي and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿فاتَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلا تَفْرَحُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿آتاكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُحِبُّ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ its object, the fāʿil being latent. ﴿مُخْتالٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَخُورٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from كل مختال. ﴿يَبْخَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ﴾ conjoined to يبخلون. ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِالْبُخْلِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and من is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and inna and its noun (ism). ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ﴾ two khabars (predicates); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رُسُلَنا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the response to the implied oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَعَهُمُ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْمِيزانَ﴾ conjoined to الكتاب. ﴿لِيَقُومَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl). ﴿النَّاسُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb — a preposition and its genitive noun — is attached to أرسلنا. ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْحَدِيدَ﴾ its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِيهِ بَأْسٌ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate) and a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿شَدِيدٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَمَنافِعُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ both attached to منافع. ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an أن concealed after the lām of reason, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَنْصُرُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من, and the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to ليقوم. ﴿وَرُسُلَهُ﴾ conjoined to the accusative pronoun. ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ both attached to the verb before them. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:26-26.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the response to the omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿نُوحاً﴾ its object. ﴿وَإِبْراهِيمَ﴾ conjoined to نوحا; the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ conjoined to أرسلنا. ﴿فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿النُّبُوَّةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْكِتابَ﴾ conjoined to النبوة.
فمنهم: the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿiyya), and the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مُهْتَدٍ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to كثير. ﴿فاسِقُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلى آثارِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿بِرُسُلِنا﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَقَفَّيْنا﴾ conjoined to the first قفينا. ﴿بِعِيسَى﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ابْنِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of عيسى, and it is muḍāf. ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ﴾ a past verb and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الْإِنْجِيلَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اتَّبَعُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿رَأْفَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَرَحْمَةً﴾ conjoined to رأفة. ﴿وَرَهْبانِيَّةً﴾ conjoined to رأفة and رحمة. ﴿ابْتَدَعُوها﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ṣifa of رهبانية. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿كَتَبْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a ṣifa of رهبانية. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ابْتِغاءَ﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿رِضْوانِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and ما is negative. ﴿رَعَوْها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿حَقَّ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿رِعايَتِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَجْرَهُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَآمِنُوا﴾ conjoined to اتقوا. ﴿بِرَسُولِهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنوا. ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كِفْلَيْنِ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of كفلين. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ﴾ conjoined to يؤتكم. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿نُوراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَمْشُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣifa of نورا. ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ﴾ conjoined to يجعل. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ﴾ the lām is for reason (taʿlīl), أن is an infinitival (maṣdarī) and accusative-governing particle, لا is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن. ﴿أَهْلُ﴾ fāʿil (agent), and it is muḍāf. ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أن﴾ lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun (ism) is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَقْدِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن, and the lightened أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in place of the two objects of يعلم. ﴿عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of شيء. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿بِيَدِ﴾ its khabar. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يُؤْتِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنْ﴾ its second object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ذُو﴾ its khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الْفَضْلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source prints this word as ﴿الْفَضْلَ﴾ with fatḥa; as muḍāf ilayhi the Quranic text has ﴿الْفَضْلِ﴾.] ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ a ṣifa of الفضل.

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): «سبّح» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; «لله» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبّح». It was also said that the lām is redundant (zāʾida) with the object. The discussion of this verb has preceded, and that it is sometimes transitive by itself and at other times with the lām. This verb came in some of the openings (of surahs) as a past verb, as in this opening, in some as an imperfect, and in some as an imperative, to indicate that these things glorify (Allah) at all times. «ما» is the fāʿil (agent) of «سبّح»; «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات». The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «العزيز» a first khabar (predicate) and «الحكيم» a second khabar. He expressed it with «ما» rather than «من» by giving precedence to the majority (taghlīb).
(لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ): «له» is a fronted khabar and «ملك السموات» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات». The clause «يحيي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «له», or resumptive. The clause «له ملك السموات» is resumptive and has no grammatical position.
(وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «قدير» its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قدير».
(هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الأول» its khabar, and what follows is conjoined to it; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «عليم» its khabar; «بكل شيء» is attached to «عليم».
(هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ): «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذي» its khabar; the clause «خلق السموات والأرض» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «في ستة أيام» is attached to «خلق»; «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «استوى» is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; «على العرش» is attached to «استوى».
(يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنْها): the clause «يعلم» is circumstantial or resumptive; «يعلم» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "هو"; «في الأرض» is attached to «يلج»; «ما يخرج منها» is conjoined to «ما يلج في الأرض»; «منها» is attached to «يخرج».
(وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها): «وما» is conjoined to the first «ما», and «ما يعرج فيها» is also conjoined.
(وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «معكم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar. «أينما» is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, and it is attached to its omitted answer. «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then He is with you"; and «كنتم» is complete (tāmma) [Translator's note: the source calls «كنتم» both defective (nāqiṣ) and complete (tāmma) here; translated as written]. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «بصير» the khabar; «بما تعملون» is attached to «بصير»; the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position.
(لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ): «له» is a fronted khabar and «ملك السموات» is its khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "its mubtadaʾ" is meant]; «إلى الله» is attached to «ترجع»; «ترجع» is a passive imperfect verb and «الأمور» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ): the clause is circumstantial or resumptive; «الليل» is the object of «يولج»; «في النهار» is attached to «يولج», and what follows is conjoined to it.
(وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «عليم» its khabar; «بذات الصدور» is attached to «عليم».

dervis-irab:7-10.t:
* I'rab:
(آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَأَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا جَعَلَكُمْ مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ): resumptive speech, set forth to begin addressing the unbelievers of Quraysh and commanding them to believe, after He had mentioned kinds of proofs of the divine oneness. «آمنوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «بالله» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنوا»; «رسوله» is conjoined to it; «أنفقوا» is conjoined to «آمنوا»; «مما» is attached to «أنفقوا»; the clause «جعلكم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the kāf is the first object and «مستخلفين» the second object of «جعل»; «فيه» is attached to «مستخلفين», i.e. of acquired wealth and gathered equipment.
(فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْفَقُوا لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «أنفقوا» is conjoined to «آمنوا», falling within the scope of the ṣila; «لهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «أجر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «كبير» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause «لهم أجر كبير» is the khabar of «الذين».
(وَما لَكُمْ لا تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a noun of disapproving interrogation, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; «لكم» is the khabar; the clause «لا تؤمنون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; «بالله» is attached to «تؤمنون». The meaning is: what thing has become settled for you while you are not believing? The wāw is circumstantial; «الرسول» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يدعوكم» is the khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the wāw in «تؤمنون».
(لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the lām is for causation; «تؤمنوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يدعوكم»; «بربكم» is attached to «تؤمنوا». The wāw is circumstantial; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «أخذ ميثاقكم» is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يدعوكم», also by way of overlapping (tadākhul) [i.e. a ḥāl within a ḥāl]. In one reading it is «أُخِذ» in the passive, so «ميثاقكم» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); i.e. His setting up proofs for you and enabling you to reflect is equivalent to taking the covenant. It was also said that it is a reference to His making them testify about themselves in His saying «ألست بربكم قالوا بلى». «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "then now the signs of certainty have appeared, the proofs and demonstrations have become clear, and the rational and transmitted arguments have become binding on you"; «مؤمنين» is the khabar of «كنتم».
(هُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلى عَبْدِهِ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ): «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذي» its khabar; the clause «ينزل» is the ṣila and has no grammatical position; «على عبده» is attached to «ينزل»; «آيات» is a mafʿūl bihi and «بيّنات» an adjective. The lām is for causation; «يخرجكم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ينزل»; «من الظلمات» is attached to «يخرجكم», i.e. from unbelief; «إلى النور» is also attached to «يخرجكم», i.e. to faith.
(وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «إنّ» and its noun; «بكم» is attached to «رءوف»; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «رءوف» is the first khabar of «إنّ» and «رحيم» the second khabar of «إنّ».
(وَما لَكُمْ أَلَّا تُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a noun of disapproving interrogation, a mubtadaʾ; «لكم» is the khabar; «أن» is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; «لا» is negating; «تنفقوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «أن»; «أن» with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in not spending" or "from not spending", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. «في سبيل الله» is attached to «تنفقوا». The wāw is circumstantial; «لله» is a fronted khabar and «ميراث السموات» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات»; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of the settling (istiqrār) or of its object; i.e. and what thing prevents you from spending in the way of Allah, while the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him?
(لا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ وَقاتَلَ): resumptive speech, set forth to explain the difference in the ranks of those who spend. «لا» is negating; «يستوي» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); «منكم» is a ḥāl; «من» is its fāʿil; the clause «أنفق» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «من قبل الفتح» is attached to «أنفق»; «قاتل» is conjoined to «أنفق». There is an omission in the speech that will be mentioned in the Rhetoric section.
(أُولئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَقاتَلُوا): «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to those who spent; «أعظم» is the khabar; «درجة» is a tamyīz (specification); «من الذين» is attached to «أعظم»; the clause «أنفقوا» is the ṣila; «من بعد» is attached to «أنفقوا»; «قاتلوا» is conjoined to «أنفقوا».
(وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى): «الله» is the fāʿil of «وعد» and «الحسنى» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «خبير» its khabar, and «بما تعملون» is attached to «خبير». [Translator's note: the source does not parse «كلا» (the first object) here, and the last part refers to the end of the verse, «والله بما تعملون خبير», which is not quoted.]

* Rhetoric:
1- Omission (al-ḥadhf): omission in these verses is frequent, and we summarise it as follows:
- The object of «أنفقوا» is omitted for intensity in urging spending and not being stingy with wealth.
- The object of «تنفقوا في سبيل الله» is omitted for the reason already given, and to intensify the rebuke, i.e. and what is with you that you do not spend what is a means of drawing near to Allah the Exalted?
- The second of the two things being equal is omitted, because equality (istiwāʾ) is only complete with two things, so a muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being: "Not equal among you are the one who spent before the conquest of Mecca and the strength of Islam and the one who spent after the conquest"; it was omitted because the indication of it is clear. Abū Ḥayyān's words on this point: "What is apparent is that «من» is the fāʿil of «لا يستوي», and its counterpart, namely «ومن أنفق من بعد الفتح وقاتل», is omitted because the meaning is clear. «أولئك», i.e. those who spent before the conquest, before Islam spread and became widespread and before the Muslims took control of the Mother of Towns (Mecca); they are the first forerunners among the Emigrants (Muhājirūn) and the Helpers (Anṣār), about whom the saying of the Prophet ﷺ came: 'If one of you were to spend the like of Uḥud in gold, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor half of it.' Far-fetched is the one who held that the fāʿil of «لا يستوي» is a pronoun referring to spending, i.e. it — spending, i.e. its genus — is not equal, since some of it is before the conquest and some after; and that «من أنفق» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is what follows it, the clause being in the position of nominative as the khabar of «من». This involves breaking up the speech and departing from the apparent sense without necessity. Omitting the conjoined element because the counterpart indicates it is frequent." Spending and fighting before the conquest were better than spending and fighting after the conquest only because the people's need was greater at that time, and they were fewer and weaker.
2- In His saying «في سبيل الله» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), i.e. obedience to Him; and the way of Allah is every good that leads them to Him.

dervis-irab:11-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(انْظُرُونا): an imperative from naẓar (looking). Naẓar is turning the eye toward the direction in which the visible thing whose seeing is intended lies. Among what indicates this is the poet's saying:
فيا ميّ هل يجزى بكائي بمثله ... مرارا وأنفاسي إليك الزوافر
وإني متى أشرف على الجانب الذي ... به أنت من بين الجوانب ناظر
(O Mayy, will my weeping be repaid with its like, time and again, and my sighs that rise toward you? Whenever I come upon the side, among all sides, where you are, I am looking.)
For if naẓar were seeing (ruʾya), he would not ask for repayment for it, because the lover does not seek any reward for looking at his beloved; rather he wants that and longs for it. Also indicating this is the other poet's saying:
ونظرة ذي شجن وامق ... إذا ما الركائب جاوزن ميلا
(And the look of a grieving, loving man when the riding camels have passed a mile.)
As for His saying, glorified is He, «ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة», the meaning is that He, glorified is He, does not grant them His mercy. You may say "So-and-so looked at me" when he grants you something, and a speaker says "Look at me, may Allah look at you", meaning "grant me good, may Allah grant you". The verb naẓartu and what is inflected from it is used in several ways:
1- The first is that you mean by it "I looked at the thing", omitting the preposition and making the verb reach the object directly. Among this is what Abū al-Ḥasan recited:
ظاهرات الجمال والحسن ينظر ... ن كما ينظر الأراك الظباء
(Of manifest beauty and loveliness, they look as the gazelles look at the arāk trees.)
The meaning is "they look at the arāk", and the preposition was omitted. For this reason Abū Ḥayyān said: "Naẓar in the sense of seeing is not transitive by itself except in poetry; it is only transitive with «إلى»."
2- The second is that you mean by it "I contemplated and considered"; it is an intransitive verb. Among this is their saying "Go and look at Zayd, whose father is he?"; by this contemplation is meant. Among this is His saying «انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال» and «انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض». This may be made transitive with a preposition, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت», which is an urging to contemplate; and it may be made transitive with «في», as in His saying «أفلم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات والأرض». As for the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فلما بدا حوران والآل دونه ... نظرت فلم تنظر بعينك منظرا
(When Ḥawrān appeared with the mirage before it, you looked, but your eye looked on no sight.)
it may be "you looked, but you did not see with your eye a sight" toward the āl, i.e. the mirage. It has also been allowed that by naẓar he meant seeing in an extended sense, because turning the sight toward the thing seen is followed by seeing, and a thing may be called by the word for what follows it and is joined to it, as in their calling the water-skin rāwiya [Translator's note: rāwiya is originally the camel that carries the water]. And "you looked but did not look" may be like "you spoke but did not speak", i.e. you did not produce speech as it was wanted; likewise "you looked but your eye did not look on a sight" as you wanted, or did not see a sight that pleases.
3- The third is that you mean by it "I waited for him". Among this is His saying «غير ناظرين إناه», and like it the saying of al-Farazdaq:
نظرت كما انتظرت الله حتى ... كفاك الماحلين لك المحالا
(I waited as you waited for Allah, until He sufficed you against those who plotted guile against you.)
He means "I waited as you waited."
4- The fourth is that anẓartu is in the sense of intaẓartu (I waited), where by your saying "anẓirnī" you seek the respite that waiting requires. Among this is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
أبا هند فلا تعجل علينا ... وأنظرنا نخبرك اليقينا
(O Abū Hind, do not be hasty against us; give us respite and we will tell you the certain truth.)
And among this is His saying «فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون»; it is only a request for respite and postponement. On this basis is the reading of Ḥamza «أَنظِرونا» with the hamza of disjunction (qaṭʿ) and the ẓāʾ with kasra.
(يُقْرِضُ): qarḍ (loan) is what you give someone else so that he repays it to you; it is cutting it off from its owner with his permission on the guarantee of returning its like. The Arabs say: "I have with you a loan of truth" and "a loan of evil" when someone has done him good or evil. The poet said:
ويقضي سلامان بن مفرج قرضها ... بما قدّمت أيديهم وأزلت
(And Salāmān ibn Mufarrij will repay its loan for what their hands sent forth and conferred.)
More on its meaning here will come in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ وَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ): there are several views on it. One of them is that «من» is interrogative, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), «ذا» is a demonstrative that is its khabar (predicate), and «الذي» is an adjective of it or a badal (substitute) for it. It is valid for «من ذا» to be an interrogative on its own, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «الذي» as its khabar. It is also valid for «ذا» to be the mubtadaʾ, «الذي يقرض الله» an adjective, and «من» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, placed before it because of the meaning of interrogation in it. «يقرض» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «الله» is its object; «قرضا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «حسنا» a naʿt (adjective). The fāʾ is causal (sababiyya); «يضاعفه» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ, as an answer to the interrogative. It was also read in the nominative, as resumption or conjunction. Abū Ḥayyān has a fine discussion here which we quote as follows: "ʿĀṣim read «فيضاعفَه» in the accusative with the fāʿ as an answer to the interrogative. There is unease in this, said Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, because the question did not fall on the lending; the question only fell on the doer of the lending, and the fāʾ only makes accusative a verb referred back to a verb being asked about. But this group — meaning of the readers — took it according to the sense, as though His saying «من ذا الذي يقرض» were equivalent to His saying 'Will anyone lend to Allah so that He multiplies it?' This view that Abū ʿAlī held — that the fāʾ only makes accusative a verb referred back to a verb being asked about — is not correct. Rather it is permissible when the interrogation is by its nominal particles, as in 'Who calls me, so that I answer him?', 'Where is your house, so that I visit you?', 'When do you travel, so that I accompany you?' and 'How will you be, so that I keep you company?'. The interrogation here concerns the person of the caller, the adverb of place, the adverb of time and the state, not the verb. Ibn Kaysān reported from the Arabs: 'Where did Zayd go, so that we follow him?', likewise 'How much is your wealth, so that we may spend it?' and 'Who is your father, so that we honour him?', with the accusative after the fāʾ. The reading «فيضاعفه» in the accusative is a mutawātir reading, and the verb occurs as the ṣila of «الذي», «الذي» is an adjective of «ذا», and «ذا» is its khabar [i.e. of «من»]. If the accusative is permissible in a case like this, its permissibility in the preceding examples is all the more fitting." «له» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضاعفه». The wāw is circumstantial; «له» is a fronted khabar and «أجر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «كريم» is an adjective.
(يَوْمَ تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ يَسْعى نُورُهُمْ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ): «يوم» is an adverb attached to the settling (istiqrār) that governs «وله أجر», i.e. a reward is settled for him on that day; or to an implied verb, its implied form being "they will be rewarded"; [or] made accusative by "remember", so that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: its governor is «فيضاعفه». The clause «ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The clause «يسعى نورهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual; «نورهم» is the fāʿil of «يسعى»; the adverb is attached to «يسعى»; «بأيمانهم» is conjoined to «أيديهم».
(بُشْراكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the clause is the speech quoted by an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "and it will be said to them". «بشراكم» is a mubtadaʾ; «اليوم» is an adverb attached to the omitted saying; «جنات» is the khabar of «بشراكم»; the clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is an adjective of «جنات»; «خالدين» is a ḥāl, and its governor is the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is "your good tidings are your entering gardens, abiding in them"; the fāʿil, namely the pronoun of the addressees, was omitted and the maṣdar (verbal noun) was annexed to its object, so it became "entering gardens"; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place in the i'rab. «فيها» is attached to «خالدين». «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «هو» a second mubtadaʾ and «الفوز» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «ذلك»; «العظيم» is an adjective of «الفوز».
(يَوْمَ يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالْمُنافِقاتُ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ): the adverb is a badal for the «يوم» before it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears to me that its governor is «ذلك هو الفوز العظيم», as if He were saying that the believers win mercy on the day when such-and-such befalls the hypocrites, because a man's triumph on the day his enemy is extinguished is more marvellous and more splendid." Abū Ḥayyān rejected this. The clause «يقول المنافقون» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; «المنافقات» is conjoined to «المنافقون»; «للذين» is attached to «يقول»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila; the clause «انظرونا» is the speech quoted (maqūl al-qawl). This is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; «نا» is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. «نقتبس» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request, i.e. we will take light; «من نوركم» is attached to «نقتبس».
(قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَراءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُوراً): «قيل» is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, referring to the believers or to the angels charged with them [Translator's note: so in the source]. «ارجعوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the speech quoted. «وراءكم» is an adverb attached to «ارجعوا», i.e. go back to the place of standing, to where we were given this light, and seek another light, since you have no way to this light. Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that «وراءكم» be a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) containing a pronoun as fāʿil, i.e. "go back, go back", and he refused that it be an adverb of «ارجعوا», saying: because of its little benefit, since going back is only ever to the rear. This is not sound. The fāʾ is a conjunction; «التمسوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «ارجعوا»; «نورا» is a mafʿūl bihi.
(فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِسُورٍ لَهُ بابٌ باطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ وَظاهِرُهُ مِنْ قِبَلِهِ الْعَذابُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ضرب» is a passive past verb; «بسور» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil. It was also said that the adverb is the nāʾib fāʿil, and it was said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) with the nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. a wall was set up between them. The clause is conjoined to His saying «قيل ارجعوا», for when the believers or the angels prevented them from catching up with them to take from their light, those hypocrites remained in a dense darkness in which the eye does not glimpse any spark from its side. More of this meaning will come in the Rhetoric section. «له» is a fronted khabar and «باب» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is an adjective of «سور». «باطنه» is a mubtadaʾ; «فيه» is a fronted khabar and «الرحمة» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «فيه [الرحمة]» is the khabar of «باطنه», and the clause is a second adjective of «سور», or an adjective of «باب»; perhaps this is preferable because of its nearness, since the pronoun refers to the nearest unless there is a contextual indication, and none is determined here. «وظاهره»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ظاهره» is a mubtadaʾ; «من قبله» is a fronted khabar and «العذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of «ظاهره», and the whole clause is conjoined to the one before it.
(يُنادُونَهُمْ: أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ): the clause «ينادونهم» is resumptive; it was also said that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in the adverb. The hamza is an interrogative particle; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) [i.e. turning the imperfect into past meaning] and jussive; «نكن» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "نحن"; «معكم» is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar. The interrogative clause is explicative and has no grammatical position, or it is in the accusative by an implied verb of saying.
(قالُوا بَلى وَلكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ وَارْتَبْتُمْ): «قالوا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «بلى» is a particle of answer; «لكنكم» is «لكنّ» and its noun; the clause «فتنتم أنفسكم» is the khabar of «لكنكم»; «تربصتم» and «ارتبتم» are conjoined to «فتنتم». The complements of the three verbs are omitted, i.e. you tempted yourselves with hypocrisy, you awaited misfortunes for the believers, and you doubted about the religion.
(وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمانِيُّ حَتَّى جاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ): the wāw is a conjunction, [followed by] a verb and its fāʿil; «حتى» is a particle of limit and of the genitive; «جاء أمر الله» is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. death; «غرّكم» is conjoined to «وغرتكم»; «بالله» is attached to «غرّكم»; «الغرور» is the fāʿil, i.e. Satan.
(فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ وَلا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. if you wish to know your end and your destinies, then today... «اليوم» is an adverb attached to «يؤخذ»; «لا» is negating; «يؤخذ» is a passive imperfect verb; «منكم» is also attached to «يؤخذ»; «فدية» is the nāʾib fāʿil. The verb is masculine because the femininity is figurative; it was also read «تؤخذ» with the tāʾ. «ولا من الذين كفروا» is conjoined to «منكم», and the clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(مَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ هِيَ مَوْلاكُمْ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ): «مأواكم النار» is a fronted khabar and a postponed mubtadaʾ, or the reverse; «هي» is a mubtadaʾ and «مولاكم» the khabar. «مولاكم» may validly be in the sense of "more fitting for you". Labīd said:
فغدت كلا الفرجين تحسب أنه ... مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها
(So she went off at dawn, thinking each of the two openings to be the proper place of fear, behind her and before her.)
It is from his Muʿallaqa, describing a wild cow. The farj is the place of fear, and what is between the legs of animals: what is between the forelegs is a farj and what is between the hind legs is a farj. Thaʿlab said that mawlā in this verse means "the more fitting for the thing", like the saying of Allah the Exalted «مأواكم النار هي مولاكم», i.e. more fitting for you. He says: that cow went off at dawn thinking that each of her two openings was the mawlā of fear, i.e. its place and its owner; or thinking that each of her two openings was the more fitting for fear, i.e. for being feared. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: by "the fear" he meant the dogs, and by its mawlā their owner; i.e. she went off not knowing whether the dogs and the dog-master [Translator's note: the source has «الكلاب والكلاب»; it may mean "the dogs and the dog-handler (kallāb)" or be a duplication] were behind her or in front of her, so she supposed each of the two directions to be a place of the dogs. The pronoun that is the noun of «أنّ» refers to «كلا», which is singular in form even though it contains the meaning of the dual; what comes after it may be construed once according to its form and another time according to its meaning, and construing according to the form is more frequent. Their illustration is: "كلا أخويك سبّني" (both your brothers insulted me — singular verb) and "كلا أخويك سبّاني" (dual verb). The poet said:
كلاهما حين جدّ الجري بينهما ... قد أقلعا وكلا أنفيهما رابي
(Both of them, when the race between them grew earnest, stopped, and each of their two noses was swelling with breath.)
He construed «أقلعا» according to the meaning of «كلا» and «رابيا» according to its form. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said «كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها» [Translator's note: the source quotes it as «كلتا الجنتين قد آتت أكلها»; the Quranic text has no «قد»], construing according to the form of «كلتا». «خلفها وأمامها» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is behind her and before her"; it may also be a badal for «كلا الفرجين», its implied form being "So she went off, each of the two openings, behind her and before her, she thinking it to be the place of fear". The real meaning of «مولاكم» is "your fitting place (maḥrākum, maqmanukum)"; one says "he is ḥarī to do such-and-such" and "he is qamīn to do it", i.e. worthy of that and deserving of it; i.e. your place of which it is said "it is more fitting for you", as it was said "he is a maʾinna of generosity", i.e. a place for a speaker's saying "indeed he is generous". So it is a noun of place, but not like other nouns of place, for those are a place of the event regardless of who it issues from; this is a likeness of the one preferred over another, which is its attribute, so the meaning of "more fitting (awlā)" is regarded in it because it is derived from it, just as maʾinna is taken from «إنّ» without being derived from it. It may also be meant that it is your helper, i.e. you have no helper but the Fire. «بئس» is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; «المصير» is the fāʿil; and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. the Fire.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا» there is a dependent explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya): He likened spending in the way of Allah to lending to Him, then omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it is likened to; what unites them is giving something for a return. The meaning of its being "goodly" is that it is free from the taints of showing off. As for the loan given to a person of wealth on condition that its equivalent be returned, it is an emphasised sunna; it may be obligatory for one in dire need, and forbidden to one who uses it to help himself to disobedience.
2- In His saying «يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم» there is a primary explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya aṣliyya): the light is a metaphor for the guidance and the good pleasure in which they are; the thing likened was omitted and the thing it is likened to was kept.
3- In His saying «خالدين فيها» after His saying «بشراكم اليوم» there is a shift (iltifāt) from address to the third person. The discussion of iltifāt has preceded many times.
4- In His saying «فضرب بينهم بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله العذاب» there are two lofty devices. The first is the representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): He likened the hypocrites' remaining in the pitch-darkness of their hypocrisy and its gloom to one between whom and the guiding light a wall has been set up that screens off every light. The second device is antithesis (al-muqābala): He matched its inside with its outside, and mercy with punishment.

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
