(يَأْنِ): the imperfect of «أنى يأني», of the pattern «رمى» [i.e. «رمى يرمي»]; it is weak (muʿtall), and the yāʾ that is its final radical was dropped because of the jussive particle, as will come in the I'rab. «أنى» means: its ināʾ, i.e. its time, has come. Ibn al-Sikkīt recited:
ألما يأن لي أن تجلّى عمايتي ... وأقصر عن ليلى بلى قد أنى لنا
(Has the time not yet come for my blindness to clear and for me to desist from Laylā? Yes, the time has come for us.)

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the hamza is for interrogation; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «يأن» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. «للذين» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, its implied form being "I mean", so it is for clarification (tabyīn); this is what Abū al-Baqāʾ chose, but there is no need for it, so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يأن». The clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position. «أن» with what falls within its scope is the fāʿil (agent) of «يأن», i.e. has the time of their hearts' humbling not drawn near, and has its time not come? Among this is the poet's saying:
ألم يأن لي يا قلب أن أترك الجهلا ... وأن يحدث الشيب المنير لنا عقلا
(Has the time not come, O heart, for me to leave folly, and for shining grey hair to produce in us some sense?)
«لذكر الله» is attached to «تخشع». The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «ذكر الله»; the clause «نزل» is the ṣila; «من الحق» is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَلا يَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَطالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَمَدُ): the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negating; «يكونوا» is conjoined to «تخشع». It is also permissible that «لا» be prohibitive, in which case this is a transition to forbidding the believers from being like those who preceded them. «يكونوا» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; the wāw is its noun and «كالذين» its khabar (predicate); the clause «أوتوا» is the ṣila; «الكتاب» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من قبل» is attached to «أوتوا»; «فطال» is conjoined to «أوتوا»; «عليهم» is attached to «طال»; «الأمد» is the fāʿil.
(فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): «فقست قلوبهم» is conjoined to «فطال عليهم الأمد». «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «منهم» is an adjective of «كثير», and for that reason it is allowable to begin with it; «فاسقون» is the khabar of «كثير».
(اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها): resumptive speech, set forth to address the believers mentioned, by way of shift (iltifāt). «اعلموا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا». «أنّ» and its noun, and the clause «يحيي الأرض» is the khabar of «أنّ»; the adverb is attached to «يحيي»; «موتها» is muḍāf ilayhi.
(قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «بيّنّا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «لكم» is attached to «بيّنّا»; «الآيات» is the object; «لعلّ» and its noun, and the clause «تعقلون» is its khabar.
(إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَالْمُصَّدِّقاتِ وَأَقْرَضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يُضاعَفُ لَهُمْ وَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ): «إنّ» and its noun; «المصدقات» is conjoined to «المصدقين»; «أقرضوا» is conjoined to the meaning of the verb in «المصدقين», because the lām [i.e. the article «ال»] is in the sense of «الذين» and the active participle is in the sense of «اصّدّقوا», as though it were said "those who gave in charity and lent". The Word of Majesty (Allah) is the mafʿūl bihi; «قرضا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «حسنا» a naʿt (adjective). «يضاعف» is a passive imperfect verb and «لهم» stands in place of the fāʿil; it is also permissible that what stands in place of the fāʿil be an implied pronoun referring to the [notion of] giving charity, and a muḍāf must then be omitted, i.e. the reward of giving charity; «لهم» is then attached to «يضاعف». The wāw is a conjunction; «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «أجر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «كريم» is an adjective. [Translator's note: the khabar of «إنّ» is not explicitly named in the source.]
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيقُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila; «بالله» is attached to «آمنوا»; «رسله» is conjoined to «الله»; «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ. «هم» may be a pronoun of separation (faṣl), with «الصدّيقون» the khabar of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar the khabar of the first. It is also permissible that «هم» be a third mubtadaʾ and «الصدّيقون» its khabar, it with its khabar being the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar the khabar of the first.
(وَالشُّهَداءُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ): «الشهداء» may be conjoined to what precedes it, so the pause at it is complete; He informed about those who believed that they are truthful ones and witnesses. It is also permissible that the wāw be resumptive and «الشهداء» a mubtadaʾ, and you have two views on its khabar: one is that it is the adverb after it, and the second is that it is His saying «لهم أجرهم». «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «أجرهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «نورهم» is conjoined to «أجرهم»; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila; «كذبوا» is conjoined to «كفروا»; «بآياتنا» is attached to «كفروا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the nearer verb is «كذبوا»]; «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «أصحاب الجحيم» its khabar.
(اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوالِ وَالْأَوْلادِ): resumptive speech, set forth to belittle this world and the insignificance of its affair. «اعلموا» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا»; «أنما» here is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa) [i.e. «ما» stops «أنّ» from governing]. «الحياة» is a mubtadaʾ and «الدنيا» an adjective of it; «لعب» is the khabar of «الحياة», and what follows is coordinated with it; «بينكم» is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of «تفاخر»; «في الأموال» is an adjective of «تكاثر».
(كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَباتُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَراهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطاماً): the kāf is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the meaning of what preceded, i.e. these attributes are established for it, likened to rain. The clause «أعجب» is an adjective of «غيث»; «الكفار» is the fronted object of «أعجب», and they are the sowers; «نباته» is the postponed fāʿil. «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يهيج» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil is "هو", referring to the plants, i.e. it dries up; the triliteral «هاج» means "dried up". «فتراه» is conjoined to «يهيج»; the fāʿil of «تراه» is "أنت" and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; «مصفرّا» is a ḥāl because the seeing is visual. «ثم يكون حطاما» is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «في الآخرة» is a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «شديد» is an adjective of «عذاب»; «مغفرة» is conjoined to «عذاب»; «من الله» is an adjective of «مغفرة»; «رضوان» is conjoined to «مغفرة». More of the secrets of this construction will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negating; «الحياة» is a mubtadaʾ and «الدنيا» an adjective of «الحياة»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «الغرور» is muḍāf ilayhi, and the annexation is explicative (bayāniyya) [Translator's note: the source does not explicitly name «متاع» as the khabar]. Ghurūr, with ḍamma, is what a person is deceived by of the enjoyment of this world.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying «اعلموا أن الله يحيي الأرض بعد موتها» there is a representative metaphor: He likened the softening of hearts by remembrance and recitation, after their hardness and their aversion to hearing the truth and acting on its commands, to the reviving of dead land by rain, in that each of them involves a thing reaching its expected perfection after being devoid of it. Or it is a representative metaphor for the reviving of the dead, in that He likened their reviving to the reviving of dead land, and that whoever is able to do the second is able to do the first; so it is fitting that hearts humble themselves at His remembrance.
2- In His saying «كمثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته» (the verse) there is also a representative metaphor: it is a likeness of the life of this world, in the speed of its passing and the smallness of its benefit, to the state of plants that rain has caused to grow, so that they stood up straight and the tillers — or the unbelievers, according to a difference among the exegetes — admired them, because both these and those are the most intense in admiring the adornment of the life of this world.
3- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): He set in antithesis, in His saying «وفي الآخرة عذاب», the punishment and the forgiveness in His saying «ومغفرة من الله ورضوان»; but it is an antithesis between one thing and two things, so it is of the type "one hardship will not overcome two eases". Its detail will come in Sūrat al-Inshirāḥ.

dervis-irab:21-25.t:
* I'rab:
(سابِقُوا إِلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to explain the causes and means of true boasting, in which it is valid to take pride. «سابقوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «إلى مغفرة» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سابقوا»; «من ربكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مغفرة».
(وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها كَعَرْضِ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ أُعِدَّتْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ): «جنة» is conjoined to «مغفرة»; «عرضها» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كعرض السموات» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse here reads «السماء»] is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is an adjective of «جنة»; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات». «أعدّت» is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هي"; the clause is a second adjective of «جنة», and it may also be resumptive. «للذين» is attached to «أعدّت»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «بالله» is attached to «آمنوا»; «رسله» is conjoined to «بالله».
(ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ): «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «فضل الله» the khabar; the clause «يؤتيه» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «يؤتيه» is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من» is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the second object; the clause «يشاء» is the ṣila of «من». «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «ذو الفضل العظيم» the khabar.
(ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها): «ما» is negating; «أصاب» is a past verb. «من مصيبة»: «من» is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «مصيبة» is genitive in form and nominative in position as the fāʿil of «أصاب»; the verb is masculine because the femininity of «مصيبة» is figurative. «في الأرض» is an adjective of «مصيبة», or attached to «أصاب», or to «مصيبة» itself. «ولا في أنفسكم» is conjoined to «في الأرض». «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). «في كتاب» is a ḥāl of «مصيبة», since it is specified by the adjective, or by governing [something] if «في الأرض» is attached to it; or [it is attached] to an omitted element, its implied form being "except that it is existing in a book", so it is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. «من قبل» is attached to what His saying «في كتاب» is attached to, i.e. except established in a book before We create it. «نبرأها» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «أن»; the fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah the Exalted; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, referring to the calamity — it was also said to the souls, and it was said to the earth. «أن» with what falls within its scope is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and the clause is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «كتاب». The pronoun in «نبرأها» refers to the calamity, or to the souls, or to the earth, or to all of that; and the meaning of «نبرأها» is "We create it".
(إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ): «إنّ» and its noun; «على الله» is attached to «يسير»; «يسير» is the khabar of «إنّ».
(لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ وَلا تَفْرَحُوا بِما آتاكُمْ): the lām is a preposition, and «كي» is a maṣdar-forming particle equivalent to «أن»; it is not for causation, because if it were so another particle of causation would not enter upon it. «لا» is negating; «تأسوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «كي», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. Its original form is «تأسيون»: the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was changed to alif, becoming «تأساون»; then two quiescent letters met, the alif and the wāw which is the fāʿil, so the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«أسي أسى», of the pattern «تعب», means he grieved, so he is «أسيّ» on the pattern faʿīl, like «حزين»." The genitive-governing lām with what falls within its scope is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "and We informed you" or "We told you"; some implied it as "We tested you". The wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negating; «تفرحوا» is conjoined to «تحزنوا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is «تأسوا»]; «بما» is attached to «تفرحوا»; the clause «آتاكم» is the ṣila. The complement of «فاتكم» and «آتاكم» is omitted, its implied form being "of blessings".
(وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ): «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا يحبّ» the khabar; «كل مختال» is the mafʿūl bihi and «فخور» an adjective.
(الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ): «الذين» is a badal (substitute) for His saying «كل مختال فخور», as though He said: He does not love those who are stingy. It may also be in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, the implied form being "for they deserve punishment"; it is also valid for it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who", or accusative for blame by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I blame". These views are all equal in preference. The clause «يبخلون» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «يأمرون» is conjoined to «يبخلون»; «الناس» is the mafʿūl bihi; «بالبخل» is attached to «يأمرون». Some considered the badal and the adjective readings far-fetched and made it a complete resumptive [speech] with no connection to what precedes it.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): the wāw is resumptive; «من» is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, a mubtadaʾ; «يتولّ» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it occurs as a nominal clause; «إنّ» and its noun; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) — in one reading it is dropped, which supports its being a [pronoun of] separation [Translator's note: the source says «فعلا» ("a verb"), evidently a slip for «فصلا» ("separation")] and not a mubtadaʾ; «الغني» is the khabar of «إنّ» and «الحميد» a second khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.
(لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «أرسلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «رسلنا» is the mafʿūl bihi; «بالبيّنات» is a ḥāl; the clause is resumptive.
(وَأَنْزَلْنا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْمِيزانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ): «أنزلنا» is conjoined to «أرسلنا»; «معهم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. and We sent down the Book in a state of its coming to be and becoming with them when it reached them on earth. «الكتاب» is the mafʿūl bihi and «الميزان» is conjoined to «الكتاب». The lām is for causation; «يقوم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; «بالقسط», i.e. with justice, is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. acting equitably and justly; you may also attach it to «يقوم». The lām and its genitive noun are attached to «أرسلنا» and «أنزلنا», because it is the cause of the sending and the sending down.
(وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أنزلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «الحديد» is the mafʿūl bihi; «فيه» is a fronted khabar and «بأس» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a ḥāl of «الحديد»; «شديد» is an adjective, i.e. in it is strength and protection — the discussion of this is long; «منافع للناس» is conjoined to «بأس شديد». Hardly any craft is free of iron.
(وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ليعلم» is conjoined to an omitted element indicated by the clause «فيه بأس شديد», so it is a cause for the causation [stated there], not a cause for the sending and the sending down. By this you know the error of the saying of some grammarians, such as al-Jalāl and others, that it is conjoined to «ليقوم». «الله» is the fāʿil and «من» the mafʿūl bihi; the clause «ينصره» is the ṣila of «من»; «رسله» is conjoined to the hāʾ, i.e. and helps His messengers as well; «بالغيب» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ of «ينصره», i.e. He being absent from them in this world. [Then] «إنّ» and its noun and its two predicates.

* Benefits:
Conjoining to the overt noun and to the pronoun: one conjoins to the overt noun and to the detached pronoun, whether nominative or accusative, and to the attached accusative pronoun, without condition, as in "قام زيد وعمرو" (Zayd and ʿAmr stood), "أنا وأنت قائمان" (I and you are standing) and "إياك والأسد" (beware of the lion). Conjoining to the attached accusative pronoun is as in «جمعناكم والأولين»: «الأولين» is conjoined to the kāf. It is not good to conjoin to the attached nominative pronoun, whether overt or latent, except after emphasising it with a detached pronoun, as in «لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم» and «اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة». Ibn Mālik pointed to this in al-Khulāṣa [the Alfiyya] with his saying:
وإن على ضمير رفع متصل ... عطفت فافصل بالضمير المنفصل
(If you conjoin to an attached nominative pronoun, separate with the detached pronoun.)

dervis-irab:26-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَقَفَّيْنا): taqfiya is placing a thing in the track of a thing, continuing in it. For this reason the endings of verse are called qawāfī (rhymes), since they follow the line in its track, continuing in another [line] according to its pattern. In al-Mukhtār: "«قفا أثره» means he followed it, and its pattern is «عدا» [i.e. «عدا يعدو»]; «قفّى على أثره بفلان» means he made So-and-so follow him; from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted «ثم قفينا على آثارهم برسلنا», and from it is rhymed speech (al-kalām al-muqaffā)."
(وَرَهْبانِيَّةً): rahbāniyya (monasticism) is excess in worship and spiritual discipline and cutting oneself off from people, attributed to the rahbān, who is the one excessive in fear, from «رهب», like khashyān from «خشي». It was also read with ḍamma [«رُهبانية»], as though attributed to ruhbān, the plural of rāhib, like rākib and rukbān. The wording of al-Qāmūs: "The rāhib is the singular of the ruhbān (monks) of the Christians; its maṣdar is rahba and rahbāniyya. Or ruhbān, with ḍamma, may be a singular, and its plural is rahābīn, rahābina and ruhbānūn. There is no monasticism in Islam: it is like castration, wearing chains, wearing sackcloth, abandoning meat and the like." The author of al-Munjid was content with saying: "Ruhbāniyya and rahbāniyya: the way of the monks", and he defined the rāhib by saying: "One who withdraws from people to a monastery seeking worship." More of its meaning will come in the I'rab section.
(كِفْلَيْنِ): two large portions. Kifl is a share; from it is the kifl that the rider takes as a safeguard, which is a cloak or the like that he wraps around [the saddle] on camels when he wants to sleep, so that it keeps him from falling; so there is in it a share of protection from falling.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً وَإِبْراهِيمَ وَجَعَلْنا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتابَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); the oath is repeated to show greater concern for the matter. «أرسلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «نوحا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «إبراهيم» is conjoined to «نوحا». «جعلنا» is conjoined to «أرسلنا»; «في ذريتهما» is in the position of the second object; «النبوة» is the first object of «جعلنا»; «الكتاب» is conjoined to «النبوة». By «الكتاب» He meant the genus, i.e. the four books.
(فَمِنْهُمْ مُهْتَدٍ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); «منهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مهتد» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» a naʿt (adjective) of «كثير», and «فاسقون» the khabar of «كثير».
(ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِرُسُلِنا): «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «قفينا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «على آثارهم» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قفينا»; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «رسلنا» is genitive in form and accusative in position.
(وَقَفَّيْنا بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ): «قفينا» is conjoined to the first «قفينا». «بعيسى»: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and «عيسى» is genitive in form and a mafʿūl bihi in position; «ابن» is a badal (substitute) and «مريم» is muḍāf ilayhi. «وآتيناه»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «آتيناه» is a verb, its fāʿil and the first mafʿūl bihi; «الإنجيل» is the second mafʿūl bihi.
(وَجَعَلْنا فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً وَرَهْبانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوها ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ): «جعلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «في قلوب» is in the position of the second object; «الذين» is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «اتبعوه», consisting of the verb, the fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi, is the ṣila (relative clause). «رأفة» is the first mafʿūl bihi and «رحمة» the second mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; «رحمة» is evidently conjoined to «رأفة», as the next paragraph itself treats it]. On «رهبانية» there are two views:
1- The first is that it is coordinated with «رأفة» and «رحمة», and the clause «ابتدعوها» is an adjective of it. It was singled out by mention of innovating only because mercy and compassion in the heart are an innate matter in which man has no acquisition, unlike monasticism, for it is among the acts of the body and man has acquisition in it.
2- The second is that it is accusative by an implied verb that the overt one explains, so the question belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun). Al-Zamakhsharī, Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and the Muʿtazila inclined to this i'rab. That is because they say: whatever is from man's act is created by him; so since compassion and mercy are from Allah's act, their creation or their being made was attributed to Him, and since monasticism is not from the act of Allah the Exalted but from the act of the servant, its creation was attributed to him.
Here, for the reader, is the text of Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "«ورهبانية» is conjoined to what precedes it, so it enters into the clauses, and the clause «ابتدعوها» is a clause in the position of an adjective of «رهبانية». Monasticism was singled out by innovating because in compassion and mercy in the heart man has no acquisition, unlike monasticism, for it is acts of the body together with something in the heart, so there is room in it for acquisition. Qatāda said: mercy is from Allah, and monasticism — they innovated it." Monasticism is rejecting this world and its desires, of women and others, and taking hermitages. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī made «ورهبانية» cut off from conjunction with what precedes it of «رأفة» and «رحمة», so for him «ورهبانية» is accusative by the implication of a verb explained by what follows it; so it is of the chapter of ishtighāl, i.e. "and they innovated monasticism — they innovated it". Al-Zamakhsharī followed him and said: "Its accusative is by an implied verb that the overt one explains, its implied form being 'and they innovated monasticism, they innovated it', meaning they originated it from themselves and vowed it." This is the i'rab of the Muʿtazila — Abū ʿAlī was a Muʿtazilī — and they say that what is created by Allah is not created by the servant; compassion and mercy are of Allah's creation, while monasticism is of man's innovation, so it is created by him. This i'rab of theirs is not good from the standpoint of the craft of Arabic, because something like this is of the kind in which the nominative as mubtadaʾ is not permissible, and beginning here with His saying «ورهبانية» is not permissible, because it is indefinite with none of the justifications for beginning with an indefinite noun.
Ibn al-Munayyir said, following up on al-Zamakhsharī: "In the i'rab of this verse Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī became entangled and sided with the faction of discord and the party of innovation: he parsed «رهبانية» as accusative by an implied verb that the overt one explains, and he gave a reason for the impossibility of conjunction, saying: 'Do you not see that monasticism cannot properly be construed with «جعلنا» while it is described by His saying «ابتدعوها», because what He, the Exalted, makes they do not innovate?' Al-Zamakhsharī too went down his blameworthy path, and his accursed devil handed him over: when he allowed what Abū ʿAlī had forbidden, namely making it conjoined, he excused that by distorting «الجعل» (making) to the meaning of granting success (tawfīq), fleeing from what Abū ʿAlī fled from — the belief that this is created by Allah the Exalted — and inclining to associating partners [with Allah] and the belief that what they themselves do Allah the Exalted does not lead astray [Translator's note: «لا يضلّه» as in the source; perhaps «لا يُحِلّه» or a similar word is meant] nor create. What is in this verse suffices as proof, after the decisive proofs and rational demonstrations, of the falsity of what the two of them believed: for the mention of the place of mercy and compassion, while it is known that their place is the accusative [Translator's note: «محلها النصب» as in the source; the sense seems to be that their place is known to be the heart], made His saying «في قلوب الذين اتبعوه» an emphasis of His creating these meanings and a depiction of the meaning of creation by mentioning its place. If what was meant were something not created in their hearts by Allah the Exalted, as the two of them claimed, His saying «في قلوب الذين اتبعوه» would have no place left, and Allah refuses that His noble Book should contain what has no place."
As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he combined the two opinions and said: "The saying of Allah the Exalted «ورهبانية» is accusative by a verb indicated by «ابتدعوها», not by conjunction with «الرحمة», because what Allah the Exalted made they do not innovate. It was also said that it is conjoined to it, and «ابتدعوها» is an adjective of it; the meaning is: He imposed on them adherence to a monasticism that they innovated; for this reason He said «ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله»."
As for Ibn Hishām, he said in al-Mughnī: "And al-Fārisī's saying about «ورهبانية ابتدعوها» that it is of the chapter of «زيدا ضربته»; Ibn al-Shajarī objected to him that the condition of the accusative noun in this chapter is that it be specified, so that its being nominative as mubtadaʾ is valid. The well-known view is that it is conjoined to what precedes it and «ابتدعوها» is an adjective, and a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. 'the love of monasticism' [Translator's note: the source has «وجد» (found), probably for «حبّ» (love) as in al-Mughnī]. Abū ʿAlī did not construe the verse in that way only because of his Muʿtazilism, so he said: because what they innovate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not create."
The summary of the dispute is that if «ورهبانية» were made conjoined to what precedes it, there would be a contradiction in the speech: the import of the speech requires that monasticism be created by Allah, while the description of it by innovation requires that it be created by them, and what is created by them Allah does not create [on their view], so it is a contradiction. Therefore al-Fārisī, followed by al-Zamakhsharī, turned away from conjunction and made it of the chapter of ishtighāl. We have cited these sayings only to show you the effect that i'rab has on directing belief; for this reason we did not see any room for ourselves to prefer [one view]; so reflect.
We return to complete the i'rab of the verse and say: the clause «ابتدعوها» is either an adjective of «رهبانية» or explicative, according to the two views. «ما» is negating; «كتبناها» is a verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is an adjective of «رهبانية» in any case; it may also be resumptive. «إلا» is a particle of exception if we consider the exception disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), or a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) if we consider it joined (muttaṣil). On the first, «ابتغاء» is parsed as a disjoined excepted noun, «إلا» being in the sense of «لكن», and the meaning is: We did not impose it on them, but they innovated it. On the second, «ابتغاء» is parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them for any reason whatsoever except for seeking the good pleasure of Allah, and «كتب» is then in the sense of "decreed". Al-Zamakhsharī was content with the first view.
(فَما رَعَوْها حَقَّ رِعايَتِها): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ما» is negating; «رعوها» is a verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi; «حق رعايتها» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «آتينا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «الذين» is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «منهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «أجرهم» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» an adjective and «فاسقون» the khabar.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ): «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; the hāʾ is for drawing attention; «الذين» is a badal; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila. «اتقوا الله» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi; «آمنوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «اتقوا»; «برسوله» is attached to «آمنوا». «يؤتكم» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and «كفلين» the second mafʿūl bihi; «من رحمته» is an adjective of «كفلين».
(وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ): conjoined to «يؤتكم»; «لكم» is attached to «يجعل» or is in the position of the second object; «نورا» is the object of «يجعل»; the clause «تمشون به» is an adjective of «نورا».
(وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): conjoined to what preceded; «لكم» is attached to «يغفر»; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «غفور» a first khabar and «رحيم» a second khabar.
(لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ أَلَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى شَيْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ): the lām is the lām of causation; «أن» is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; «لا» is redundant; «يعلم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «أن», i.e. so that [they] may know your deeds by that [Translator's note: «أي ليعلم أعمالكم بذلك» as in the source]; so the lām is attached to an omitted element drawn from the meaning of the request clause. «أهل الكتاب» is the fāʿil of «يعلم». «أن» is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); «لا» is negating; the clause «يقدرون» is the khabar of «أن», and the meaning is "that they are not able". «على شيء» is attached to «يقدرون»; «من فضل الله» is an adjective of «شيء»; «أن» with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «يعلم».
(وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope is conjoined to «أن لا يقدرون», falling within the scope of what is known. «أنّ» and its noun; «بيد الله» is the khabar of «أنّ»; the clause «يؤتيه» is resumptive or a second khabar of «أنّ»; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and «من» the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause «يشاء» is the ṣila.
(وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ): «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «ذو الفضل» its khabar and «العظيم» an adjective of «الفضل».

* Benefits:
A negation may intervene in the speech, and then «أن» must be made overt after the lām of causation to which «لا» is attached. If «أن» were implied here it would not be permissible, because implying it would lead to the preposition directly adjoining the particle of negation, and that is not permissible.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُوَ ٱلأَوَّلُ﴾.
He means: before everything. ﴿وَٱلآخِرُ﴾: after everything.
﴿وَٱلظَّاهِرُ﴾: over everything in knowledge; and likewise ﴿وَٱلْبَاطِنُ﴾: over everything in knowledge.

farraa:7-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا جَعَلَكُم مُّسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ﴾: (of what He has) given you possession of, and that is His provision and His gift.
All the readers are for: ﴿وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثَاقَكُمْ﴾; had it been read «وقد أُخِذَ ميثاقكم» (passive), it would have been correct.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿فَيُضَاعِفَهُ لَهُ﴾.
It is read in the nominative and in the accusative. Whoever makes it nominative makes the fāʾ a conjunction, not an answer (jawāb), as in your saying: «من ذا الذى يحسن ويجمل؟» (Who is it that does well and behaves finely?). Whoever makes it accusative makes it an answer to the question. In questions the Arabs join «مَن» to «ذا» until they become like a single word; and I have seen it in some of the codices of ʿAbd Allāh as «منذا», joined in writing, just as ﴿يَابْنَ أُمَّ﴾ is joined in our script and in the script of ʿAbd Allāh.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْعَىٰ نُورُهُم بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, that is: it shines before them, and on their right and on their left. The bāʾ in "بأيمانهم" has the meaning of «فى» (in), and likewise of «عن».
And His saying: ﴿بُشْرَاكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ﴾.
You make «البشرى» and «الجنات» nominative. Had you intended «البشرى» to be accusative, making the angels' announcing fall upon it — as though it were said to them: «rejoice in your good tidings» — you would then make «جناتٍ» accusative, with «البشرى» falling upon it.
And if you wish, you make it accusative by «qaṭʿ» (detachment), because it is indefinite, from the description of a definite noun. Or you make «البشرى» nominative by «اليوم», as in your saying «اليوم بشراكم، اليوم سروركم» (today is your good tidings, today is your joy), then make «الجنات» accusative by qaṭʿ; and in this sense «اليوم» may be nominative or accusative, as the poet said:
زَعم البوارِحُ أنَّ رِحلتنا غدا * وبذاك خبرنا الغُدافُ الأسود
(The ill-omened birds claimed that our departure is tomorrow, and of that the black raven informed us.)
And His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَوْزُ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is "ذلك الفوز العظيم", without «هو».
In our reading it is "ذلك هو الفوز العظيم", just as in our reading there is "فإنَّ اللهَ هُو الغَنِىّ الحميد" (24), while in the codex of the people of Medina it is "فإن الله الغنى الحميد".

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it (أَنْظِرُونا), from «أنظرت»; and the rest of the readers are for (انْظُرُونَا), with a light (connecting) alif. The meaning of «انظرُونا» is:
wait for us; and the meaning of «أنظِرونا» is: grant us respite, as He said: ﴿أَنْظِرْنى إلى يوم يُبعثون﴾. The Arabs also say "أَنظِرْنى" meaning «انتظرنى» (wait for me), which strengthens the reading of Yaḥyā. The poet said:
أبا هندٍ فلا تَعْجَل علينا * وأَنْظِرنا نُخَبِّرْك اليقِينا
(O Abū Hind, do not be hasty with us; wait for us and we will tell you the certain truth.)
The meaning of this is: wait for us a little and we will tell you; for there is no deferment here, only listening, as when you say to a man: «listen to me until I tell you». And His saying: ﴿قِيلَ ٱرْجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمْ﴾.
The believers said to the disbelievers: go back to the place where we took [193/ب] the light, and seek the light there. When they went back, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, set up between them — between the believers and the disbelievers — a wall, and that is the wall on which the people of al-Aʿrāf will be.
And His saying: ﴿لَّهُ بَابٌ بَاطِنُهُ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةُ﴾: Paradise; ﴿وَظَاهِرُهُ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾: the Fire. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ظاهرة من تلقائه العذاب».
«[Translator's note: «ظاهرة» is as printed, presumably for «ظاهره».]»

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿يُنَادُونَهُمْ أَلَمْ نَكُن مَّعَكُمْ﴾: upon your religion in the world. The believers said: ﴿بَلَىٰ وَلَـٰكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنتُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ لاَ يُؤْخَذُ مِنكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ﴾.
The readers are for the yāʾ; some of the people of the Hijaz said «[لا] تؤخذ» (with tāʾ). «الفدية» is derived from «الفداء». When the verb comes before «الفدية», «الشفاعة», «الصيحة», «البينة» and the like, you may make its verb feminine or masculine; the Book has come with all of that.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿مَأْوَاكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ هِيَ مَوْلاَكُمْ﴾, that is: it is more fitting for you.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن تَخْشَعَ﴾.
There are dialectal forms of «يأن»: some of the Arabs say «ألم يأن لك» and «ألم يئن لك», like «يَعِنْ»; some of them say «ألم يَنَلْ لك» with lām; and some of them say «ألم يُنلْ لك». The best of them is the one the Quran has brought. And His saying: ﴿وَمَا نَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and some of the people of Medina read it (نزَّل) with shadda, and some of them read it "وما نَزَل" without shadda. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وما أنزل من الحق»; this is support for whoever read «نزّل».
«[Translator's note: «(نزَل) مشددة» is as printed, with the shadda not shown on the word itself.]»
And His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَكُونُواْ﴾.
It is in the position of an accusative; its meaning is: has the time not come for them that their hearts should be humbled, and that they should not be like those who were given the Book? Had it been jussive, as a prohibition, it would have been correct.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَٱلْمُصَّدِّقَاتِ﴾.
ʿĀṣim read it «إنّ المصَدِّقين والمصَدِّقات» with the ṣād light (undoubled), meaning: those who believed Allah and His Messenger. Others read it «إن المصَّدّقين», meaning «المتصدقين» (the almsgivers), with shadda. In the reading of Ubayy it is «إن المتصدقين والمتصدقات», with an overt tāʾ; this is support for whoever read «إن المصّدّقين» with shadda.
«[Translator's note: «لم قرأ» is as printed, evidently for «لمن قرأ».]»

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصِّدِّيقُونَ﴾: the statement ends at the description of the truthful (al-ṣiddīqūn).
Then He said: ﴿وَٱلشُّهَدَآءُ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, meaning the prophets: they have their reward and their light. So you make «الصديقين» nominative by «هم», and you make «الشهداء» nominative by His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ﴾.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانٌ﴾.
He mentioned what is in this world and that it is as He described; as for the Hereafter, it is either punishment or Paradise. The wāw in it is a wāw with the force of one (i.e. of «أو», "or"), as in your saying: «ضع الصدقة فى كل يتيم وأرملة» (give the alms to every orphan and widow); and if you say «فى كل يتيم أو أرملة» (every orphan or widow), the meaning is the same. And Allah knows best.

farraa:22-23.t:
His saying: ﴿مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ﴾.
That is: no misfortune befalls a human being on earth, such as loss of wealth, hardship, hunger and fear; ﴿وَلاَ فِيۤ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾: death among children and others, and illnesses; ﴿إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ﴾: He means: in the primal knowledge, «من قبل أن نبرأها»: before We bring that soul into being, that is, create it. «إن ذلك على الله يسير»: then He is saying: keeping account of that for all [194/ا] creatures is easy for Allah. Then He instructed His servants, saying: this is ﴿لِّكَيْلاَ تَأْسَوْاْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمْ﴾, that is: so that you do not grieve; ﴿وَلاَ تَفْرَحُواْ بِمَآ آتَاكُمْ﴾. Whoever reads «بما أتاكم» without the long vowel makes the verb belong to «ما» (i.e. "what has come to you").

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبُخْلِ﴾.
These are the Jews: they were stingy, out of envy, about making known the description of the Prophet ﷺ, out of envy of Islam, because it would take away their dominion.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْغَنِيُّ ٱلْحَمِيدُ﴾.
In the reading of the people of Medina it is without «هو»; that is evidence for that.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنزَلْنَا ٱلْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ﴾.
It has been mentioned that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the «القلاة», the tongs and the hammer. Al-Farrāʾ said: «القلاة» is the anvil.
And His saying: ﴿فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ﴾.
He means weapons for fighting; and benefits for people, such as the knife, the axe, «المز» and the like.
«[Translator's note: «المز» is as printed and appears to be corrupt.]»

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلنُّبُوَّةَ﴾.
In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is with yāʾ, with two yāʾs: «النِّبييّة», with two bāʾs. The hamza in his script is always written with alif, of every kind; so had it been a hamza, it would have been written with alif, and had it been (on the pattern) «الفعولة», it would have been with wāw. It must be either a maṣdar of «النبأ», or «النبيّية» as a maṣdar attributed (by the nisba ending) to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Arabs say: «فعَل ذلك فى غُلوميته» (he did that in his boyhood), «فى غلومته» and «فى غلاميته». Al-Kisāʾī heard the Arabs say: «فعل ذلك فى وليديته» (he did that in his infancy), meaning: while he was a «ليد», that is, newborn. So whatever maṣdar comes to you from a primary (non-derived) noun, you may have in it «الفُعولة», «الفُعولية», or make it attributive (with nisba) on the form of the noun. Of that is your saying: «عبد بين العبودية، والعبودة، والعبدية» (a slave of evident slavery); so make analogy on this.
«[Translator's note: «بباءين» (with two bāʾs) is as printed, evidently a slip for «بياءين» (with two yāʾs); «ليد» is likewise as printed, evidently for «وليد».]»

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِن رَّحْمَتِهِ﴾.
«الكفل» is a share. Originally it is what the rider fastens behind him, which holds him and keeps him from falling. He is saying: the «كفل» will protect you from the punishment of Allah, just as the «كفل» protects this rider from falling.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «لكى يعلم أهل الكتَاب ألا يقدرون». The Arabs make «لا» a ṣila (redundant connective) in any statement at whose end a negation comes, or in an unexpressed negation. This is among those whose end a negation has entered, so (لا) at its beginning was made a ṣila. As for the preceding, unexpressed negation, it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما مَنَعكَ ألاّ تسجُدَ﴾,
and His saying: ﴿ومَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّها إِذَا جاءَتْ لا يُؤمِنُون﴾,
and His saying: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلى قَرْيةٍ أهْلَكْناهَا أنّهُم لا يَرْجِعُون﴾.
In «الحرام» there is the meaning of negation and prevention, and likewise in His saying (وما يشعركم); for that reason (لا) after it was made a ṣila, its meaning being that it drops out of the statement.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تخشع» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يأنِ»; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ذِكْر»; the clause «ولا يكونوا» is conjoined to the clause «تخشع»; the preposition phrase «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أوتوا»; the clause «فطال» is conjoined to the clause «أوتوا»; «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «فاسقون» is its khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is qualified by «منهم»; and the clause «وكثير منهم فاسقون» is conjoined to the clause «قست قلوبهم».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (أن الله يحيي الأرض) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the clause «قد بيَّنَّا» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «لعلكم تعقلون».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «وأقرضوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the active participle «المصدقين». «قرضا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the maṣdar (verbal noun) being إقراض; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «يضاعف» is the preposition phrase «لهم»; and the clause «ولهم أجر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the pronoun in «لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The wāw is a conjunction; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «أولئك هم الصدِّيقون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين», and the clause made of the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إن المصدقين يضاعف لهم»; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). «عند» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الشهداء»; the clause «لهم أجرهم» is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ «الذين»; and the clause «والذين كفروا ...» is conjoined to the clause «الذين آمنوا ...».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of أنَّ and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the adverb «بينكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar «تفاخر»; the preposition phrase «في الأموال» is attached to the maṣdar (تكاثر); the preposition phrase «كمثل» is attached to an omitted second khabar (predicate) of «الحياة»; the clause «أعجبَ نباته» is a naʿt (adjective) of «غيث»; the clause «ثم يهيج» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أعجب»; «مصفرًّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «ثم يكون» is conjoined to the clause «تراه»; the clause «وفي الآخرة عذاب» is conjoined to the maṣdar «أنما الحياة لعب», as in: «اعلم أنما زيد مجتهد وفي عمله خير» ("know that Zayd is only diligent, and in his work there is good"). The clause «وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The preposition phrase «من ربكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مغفرة»; the clause «عَرْضها كعرض» is a naʿt of «جنة»; the clause «أعدَّت» is a second naʿt of «جنة»; the clause «ذلك فضل» is resumptive; and the clause «يؤتيه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فضل».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: His words «من مصيبة»: it is the fāʿil (agent), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida); the object is omitted, i.e.: no calamity befell you [«ما أصابكم مصيبة»]; the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مصيبة»; the preposition phrase «في كتاب» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مصيبة», even though it is indefinite, because it is specified by the qualification; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition phrase «من قبل» is attached to a naʿt of «كتاب»; the preposition phrase «على الله» is attached to «يسير».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «لكيلا تأسوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, i.e.: We informed you of that; the preposition phrase «على» is attached to «تأسوا»; and the clause «والله لا يحب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: [they are] punished (مُعَذَّبون); the conditional clause is resumptive; «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «لقد أرسلنا» is the answer to the oath; the preposition phrase «بالبينات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلنا»; the clause «وأنزلنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أرسلنا»; the clause «فيه بأس» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحديد»; the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «وليعلم» is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar «ليقوم», i.e.: We have sent Our messengers, and sent down with them the Book, so that people may uphold [justice] and so that Allah may know; the preposition phrase «بالغيب» is attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in «ينصره».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The wāw is a conjunction; the clause «لقد أرسلنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا} in the preceding verse; the preposition phrase «في ذريتهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) second object; the clause «فمنهم مهتد» is conjoined to the clause «جعلنا»; his words «مهتد»: a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ and «فاسقون» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «كثير»; and the clause «وكثير منهم فاسقون» is conjoined to the clause «منهم مهتد».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «قَفَّينا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جعلنا»; the preposition phrase «في قلوب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل»; «رهبانية» is a noun conjoined to «رحمة». The clause «ابتدعوها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رهبانية», and the clause «ما كتبناها» is a second naʿt of «رهبانية»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «ابتغاء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the clause «فما رعوها» is conjoined to the clause «كتبناها». «حق» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause «فآتينا» is conjoined to the clause «ما رعوها»; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw; «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «فاسقون»; the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to a naʿt of «كثير»; and the clause «وكثير منهم فاسقون» is conjoined to the clause «آتينا».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «الذين» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); «يؤتكم» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the preposition phrase «من رحمته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كِفْلين»; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to the second object; and the clause «تمشون» is a naʿt of «نورا».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يُؤْتِكُمْ}; «أنْ» is lightened from the heavy [أنَّ], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «يقدرون» is the khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; the preposition phrase «مِنْ فضل» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء»; the second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first maṣdar; the clause «يؤتيه» is a second khabar of «أن»; and the clause «والله ذو الفضل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: His words «لله»: this lām is causal, a preposition attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبِّح». «ما» is a relative, the fāʿil (agent) of «سبح»; the clause «وهو العزيز» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the Name of Majesty.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «له ملك» is resumptive; the clause «يحيي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «له»; the clause (وهو قدير) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يحيي»; and the preposition «على كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قدير».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «هو الأول» is resumptive, and the clause (وهو عليم) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «هو الذي» is resumptive; the clause «يعلم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «استوى»; the clause «وهو معكم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «هو الذي». «أين» is a conditional noun, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida); the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «أين ما كنتم» is parenthetical between the two conjoined clauses, and the clause «والله بصير» is conjoined to the clause «هو معكم».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «له ملك» is resumptive, and the clause «تُرجع» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «له ملك».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «يولج» is resumptive; the clause «وهو عليم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يولج»; the preposition «بذات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنفقوا»; «مستخلفين» is the second object; the preposition «فيه» is attached to «مستخلفين». The clause «فالذين ... » is resumptive; the preposition «منكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «آمنوا»; and the clause «لهم أجر» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), i.e. "what thing is settled for you, not believing?" The clause «لا تؤمنون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لكم»; the clause «والرسول يدعوكم» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم»; the clause «وقد أخذ» is a ḥāl from «ربكم». The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are believers, then what prevents you from believing?"

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليخرجكم» is genitive (majrūr) and attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُنزل»; the clause «وإن الله لرءوف» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «هو الذي»; the preposition «بكم» is attached to «رؤوف».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the maṣdar (verbal noun) «ألا تنفقوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition (في). The clause «ولله ميراث» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent and object of the notion of being (istiqrār), i.e. "what thing prevents you from spending, when the inheritance of the heavens and the earth is His?" The clause «لا يستوي» is resumptive, as is the clause «أولئك أعظم»; «درجة» is a tamyīz (specification); the preposition «من الذين» is attached to «أعظم». His words «وكلا»: the wāw is conjunctive; «كلا» is the second object of «وَعَد», placed first, and the clause «وعد» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أولئك أعظم». The clause «والله خبير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «من» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a demonstrative, khabar (predicate); «الذي» is a badal (substitute) from «ذا». The fāʾ is causative (sababiyya), and the verb is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to a maṣdar drawn from the preceding speech, i.e. "is there a lending from you to Allah, and so a multiplying from Him for you?" The clause «وله أجر» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «له».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the notion of being (istiqrār) to which the earlier {لَهُ} is attached. The clause «يسعى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المؤمنين»; «بين» is an adverb of place attached to «يسعى». The clause «بشراكم جنات» is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying) of an implied saying, i.e. "the angels will say", and the implied clause is resumptive; «اليوم» is an adverb of time attached to the implied saying. The preposition «فيها» is attached to «خالدين». The clause «ذلك هو الفوز» is resumptive; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «يوم» is a badal (substitute) from the earlier {يَوْمَ}, and the clause «نقتبس» is the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition. The clause «قيل» is resumptive, and the clause «فضرب» is resumptive. The clause «له باب» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سور»; the clause «باطنه فيه الرحمة» is a naʿt of «باب», and the clause «فيه الرحمة» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «باطنه». The clause «وظاهره من قبله العذاب» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «باطنه فيه الرحمة», and the clause «مِنْ قِبله العذاب» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «ظاهره».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «ينادونهم» is resumptive, and the clause «ألم نكن معكم» is explicative of the calling. The clause «قالوا» is resumptive; the clause «بلى» (كنتم معنا) is the maqūl al-qawl (content of the saying), and the clause «ولكنكم فتنتم» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied maqūl al-qawl. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن جاء أمر الله) is genitive by «حتى» and attached to (mutaʿalliq) «غَرَّتكم», and «الغرور» is the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: His words «فاليوم»: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يؤخذ»; the preposition «منكم» is attached to the verb. The clause «مأواكم النار» is resumptive; the clause «هي مولاكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النار»; and the clause «وبئس المصير» is resumptive, the one specified [for blame] being omitted, i.e. "the Fire".

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, مَا فِي السَّمَوَات وَالْأَرْض: i.e. "and what is in the earth" (وما في الأرض); then ما was omitted, on the basis that it is an indefinite described ما (nakira mawṣūfa) whose adjective, namely في الأرض, has taken its place. It is not good for ما to mean الذي and be omitted, because the ṣila (relative clause) does not take the place of the thing described according to the Basrans, while the adjective takes the place of the thing described according to all. So construing it according to consensus is better than construing it according to a disputed view.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying الَّذِي لَهُ ملك السَّمَوَات: الذي is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it, or in the position of the accusative by [an implied] أعني ("I mean").
His saying وَهُوَ مَعكُمْ: معكم is accusative as an adverb, and the governing word in it is the meaning; its implied form is "and He is a witness with you" (وهو شاهد معكم).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying وَمَا لكم لَا تؤمنون: ما is a mubtadaʾ (subject), لكم the khabar (predicate), and لا تؤمنون a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying وكلا وعد الله: كلا is accusative by وعد. Whoever reads it in the nominative makes وعد an adjective of كل, so it does not govern it, and he puts it in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "those — each Allah has promised the best" (أولئك كل وعد الله الحسنى). Some grammarians disallowed وعد being an adjective of كل, because it is definite, its implied form being كلهم; so the khabar (predicate) can only be وعد [with an omitted referring pronoun], and that is far-fetched, not permissible according to Sībawayh except in poetry.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying مَن ذَا الَّذِي يقْرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه لَهُ: its mention has preceded in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
His saying قرضا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came not on the form of the maṣdar [of its verb], as He said أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا, and as they said أجابه جابة. It is also said that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as if He said "lends Allah lawful wealth" (يقرض الله مالا حلالا).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying يَوْم ترى: يوم is accusative, and the governing word in it is وله أجر. ويسعى is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because ترى is from seeing with the eye.
His saying بشراكم: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and جنات is its khabar (predicate); its implied form is "your good tidings are the entry into gardens" (بشراكم دخول جنات); then the muḍāf was omitted, and its meaning is that this will be said to them. Al-Farrāʾ permitted جنات in the accusative as a ḥāl, with اليوم the khabar of بشراكم; but جنات being a ḥāl has no sense, since there is no sense of a verb in it. He also permitted بشراكم to be in the position of the accusative in the sense of "they give them the good tidings", with جنات accusative by البشرى. All of it is far-fetched, because it separates between the ṣila (relative-like complement) and what it completes by اليوم.
His saying خَالِدين فِيهَا: accusative as a ḥāl of the كاف and the ميم.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying يَوْم يَقُول: يوم is an adverb, and the governing word in it is ذلك هو الفوز; it is also said that it is a badal (substitute) of the first اليوم.
His saying فَضرب بَينهم بسور: the بـ is redundant (zāʾida), and سور is in the position of the nominative, an object whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). And the بـ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a striking with a wall" (ضربا بسور). [Translator's note: the two statements about the بـ are as in the source.]

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying وَمَا نزل من الْحق: ما means الذي and is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ذكر; in نزل is the pronoun of the fāʿil (agent) referring back to ما. It is not permissible for ما with the verb to be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the verb would remain without an agent. Whoever reads نزّل with doubling puts in نزّل the name of Allah, exalted be His mention, as a latent pronoun, and assumes an omitted هاء referring back to ما, because when the verb was doubled it became transitive to an object.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying وَالشُّهَدَاء: nominative, conjoined to الصديقين, and لهم أجرهم ونورهم refers back to all of them. It is also said that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and عند ربهم the khabar (predicate); and لهم أجرهم is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar of الشهداء if you wish, the pronoun referring back to the martyrs only.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying اعلموا أَنما الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا: أنّ stands in place of the two objects of علم, and ما is the restraining ما (kāffa), because it restrains [أنّ] from governing; الحياة is a mubtadaʾ (subject), لعب the khabar (predicate), and الدنيا in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الحياة.
His saying كَمثل غيث: the كاف is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of تفاخر, or as a khabar after a khabar of الحياة.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying عرضهَا كعرض: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جنة; likewise أعدت is also a naʿt of the Garden.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying مَا أصَاب من مُصِيبَة فِي الأَرْض: His saying في الأرض is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of المصيبة according to its position, because من is redundant (zāʾida); it may also be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) according to the wording. In the adjective there is a pronoun referring back to the thing described. It is also possible that في الأرض is an adverb for أصاب or for المصيبة, and then there is no pronoun in it.
His saying تبرأها: the pronoun refers back to the affliction (المصيبة); it is also said: to the earth; and it is also said: to the souls. [Translator's note: «تبرأها» is as printed in the edition; the Quranic word is نبرأها.]

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying الَّذين يَبْخلُونَ: الذين is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), [or] as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar (predicate) omitted, or in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of كل, or by [an implied] أعني ("I mean").
His saying فِيهِ بَأْس شَدِيد: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحديد.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying أَلا ابْتِغَاء رضوَان الله: ابتغاء is an exception not of the same kind as the first (disconnected exception); it may also be a badal (substitute) of the accusative attached pronoun in كتبناها.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿سبح لله ما في السماوات والأرض﴾: «سبح» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; «لله»: the lām is a preposition, and the Word of Majesty is a genitive noun, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبح»; and it has been said: the lām is redundant (ṣila) with the object. «ما» is a relative noun in the position of a nominative, the fāʿil (agent) of «سبح». «في السماوات» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. «الأرض» is conjoined to «السماوات».
﴿وهو العزيز الحكيم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or resumptive; «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «العزيز» is a first khabar (predicate), and «الحكيم» is a second khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت﴾: «له» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «ملك السماوات» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الأرض» is conjoined to «السماوات». The clause «يحيي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «له», or resumptive, with no grammatical position; and the clause «له ملك السماوات» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وهو على كل شيء قدير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is the mubtadaʾ, and «قدير» is its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قدير».

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿هو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن﴾: «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «الأول» is its khabar (predicate), and what comes after it is conjoined to it.
﴿وهو بكل شيء عليم﴾: «هو» is the mubtadaʾ, «عليم» is its khabar, and «بكل شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿هو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض﴾: «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «الذي» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause «خلق السماوات والأرض» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿في ستة أيام﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلق».
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay.
﴿استوى﴾: a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah.
﴿على العرش﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «استوى».
﴿يعلم ما يلج في الأرض﴾: the clause «يعلم» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or resumptive, with no grammatical position; «يعلم» is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being «هو» (He); «في الأرض» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يلج».
﴿وما يخرج منها﴾: conjoined to «ما يلج في الأرض»; «منها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يخرج».
﴿وما ينزل من السماء وما يعرج فيها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is conjoined to the first «ما», and «ما يعرج فيها» is also conjoined.
﴿وهو معكم أين ما كنتم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is the mubtadaʾ; «معكم» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to an omitted khabar; «أينما» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place, and it is attached to its omitted apodosis; «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. «فهو معكم» (then He is with you); and «كنتم» is complete (tāmma). [Translator's note: the source first calls «كنتم» defective (nāqiṣ) and then complete (tāmma); both are translated as written.]
﴿والله بما تعملون بصير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «الله» is the mubtadaʾ, «بصير» is the khabar; «بما تعملون» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «بصير»; and the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿ملك السماوات﴾: its mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿والأرض﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf), genitive (majrūr).
﴿وإلى الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «ترجع».
﴿ترجع﴾: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive).
﴿الأمور﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل﴾: the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or resumptive, with no grammatical position; «الليل» is the object of «يولج»; «في النهار» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يولج»; and what comes after it is conjoined to it.
﴿وهو عليم بذات الصدور﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «عليم» is its khabar (predicate), and «بذات الصدور» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «عليم».

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿آمنوا بالله ورسوله وأنفقوا مما جعلكم مستخلفين فيه﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «آمنوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنوا», and «رسوله» is conjoined to it; «أنفقوا» is conjoined to «آمنوا»; «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أنفقوا»; the clause «جعلكم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The kāf is the first object, and «مستخلفين» is the second object of «جعل»; «فيه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «مستخلفين».
﴿فالذين آمنوا منكم وأنفقوا لهم أجر كبير﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «أنفقوا» is conjoined to «آمنوا», falling within the scope of the ṣila; «لهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «أجر» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «كبير» is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause «لهم أجر كبير» is the khabar of «الذين».

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وما لكم لا تؤمنون بالله والرسول يدعوكم﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «ما» is a noun of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī) in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لكم» is the khabar (predicate); the clause «لا تؤمنون» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تؤمنون»; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «الرسول» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «يدعوكم» is the khabar; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl from the wāw in «تؤمنون».
﴿لتؤمنوا بربكم وقد أخذ ميثاقكم﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl); «تؤمنوا» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يدعوكم»; «بربكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تؤمنوا»; the wāw is circumstantial; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «أخذ ميثاقكم» is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يدعوكم».
﴿إن كنتم مؤمنين﴾: «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, its implied form being: «فالآن ظهرت ووضحت الدلائل والبراهين» (then now the indications and proofs have appeared and become clear); and «مؤمنين» is the khabar of «كنتم».

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿هو الذي ينزل على عبده آيات بينات ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور﴾: «هو» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الذي» is its khabar (predicate); the clause «ينزل» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «على عبده» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينزل»; «آيات» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «بينات» is a ṣifa (adjective). The lām is causal (taʿlīl); «يخرجكم» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ينزل»; «من الظلمات» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يخرجكم», i.e. from disbelief; and «إلى النور» is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to «يخرجكم».
﴿وإن الله بكم لرءوف رحيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the Word of Majesty is its noun; «بكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «رؤوف»; [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «رءوف» is the first khabar of «إن», and «رحيم» is the second khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وما لكم ألا تنفقوا في سبيل الله ولله ميراث السماوات والأرض﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a noun of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لكم» is the khabar (predicate); «أن» is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, «لا» is negative, and «تنفقوا» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن». The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. «في ألا تنفقوا» (in not spending), or «من ألا تنفقوا» (from spending); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). «في سبيل الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تنفقوا»; and the clause «وما لكم...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «لله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «ميراث السماوات» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «الأرض» is conjoined to «السماوات»; the clause is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of the [implied] being (al-istiqrār), or from its object, i.e. what thing prevents you from spending in the way of Allah, when the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him?
﴿لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «لا» is negative; «يستوي» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); «منكم» is a ḥāl; «من» is its fāʿil; the clause «أنفق» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «من قبل الفتح» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أنفق»; and «قاتل» is conjoined to «أنفق».
﴿أولئك أعظم درجة من الذين أنفقوا من بعد وقاتلوا﴾: «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to «من أنفق»; «أعظم» is the khabar; «درجة» is a tamyīz (specification); «من الذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أعظم»; the clause «أنفقوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «من بعد» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أنفقوا»; and «قاتلوا» is conjoined to «أنفقوا».
﴿وكلا وعد الله الحسنى والله بما تعملون خبير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «كلا» is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «وعد», placed before it; «الله» is the fāʿil of «وعد», and «الحسنى» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «خبير» is its khabar, and «بما تعملون» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «خبير».

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا﴾: there are several views on it. The first: «من» is interrogative, in a nominative position as mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a demonstrative, its khabar (predicate); and «الذي» is a ṣifa (adjective) of it, or a badal (substitute) of it. Or «من ذا» is an interrogative on its own, in a nominative position as mubtadaʾ, and «الذي» is its khabar. Or «ذا» is a mubtadaʾ, «الذي يقرض الله» is a ṣifa, and «من» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, placed before it because of the meaning of interrogation it contains. «يقرض» is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «الله»: the Word of Majesty is its object; «قرضًا» stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); and «حسنًا» is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿فيضاعفه له وله أجر كريم﴾: the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya); «يضاعفه» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the fāʾ, in answer to the interrogation; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar gleaned from the preceding speech, i.e. «أثمة إقراض منكم لله فمضاعفة منه لكم؟» (is there a lending from you to Allah, and so a multiplying from Him for you?). «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضاعفه»; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «أجر» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «كريم» is a ṣifa.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿يوم ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم﴾: «يوم» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [implied] being (al-istiqrār) that governs «له أجر», or attached to an implied (muḍmar) verb, its implied form being «يؤجرون» (they are rewarded), or attached to «يضاعفه»; or it is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر» (remember). The clause «ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «يسعى نورهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual; «نورهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يسعى»; «بين» is an adverb attached to «يسعى»; and «بأيمانهم» is conjoined to «أيديهم».
﴿بشراكم اليوم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك هو الفوز العظيم﴾: the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an omitted [verb of] saying. «بشراكم» is the mubtadaʾ (subject); «اليوم» is an adverb attached to the omitted saying; «جنات» is the khabar (predicate) of «بشراكم»; the clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «جنات»; «خالدين» is a ḥāl, and what governs it is the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is «بشراكم دخولكم جنات خالدين فيها» (your good tidings are your entering gardens, abiding in them): the fāʿil, which is the pronoun of the one addressed, was omitted, and the maṣdar was annexed to its object, so it became «دخول جنات»; then the muḍāf was omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place in i'rab. «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «خالدين»; «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «الفوز» is its khabar, the clause being the khabar of «ذلك»; and «العظيم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الفوز».

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿يوم يقول المنافقون والمنافقات للذين آمنوا انظرونا نقتبس من نوركم﴾: the adverb (ẓarf) is a badal (substitute) of the earlier «يوم»; and it has been said: what governs it is «ذلك هو الفوز العظيم», as if He were saying: the believers attain mercy on the day when such and such befalls the hypocrites.
