The clause «يقول المنافقون» is in the position of a genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; «المنافقات» is conjoined to «المنافقون»; «للذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقول»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the clause «انظرونا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying), and this is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent) and «نا» an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «نقتبس» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), because it is the answer to the request, i.e. we take light; and «من نوركم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «نقتبس».
﴿قيل ارجعوا وراءكم فالتمسوا نورا﴾: «قيل» is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to the believers, or to the angels charged with them. «ارجعوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. «وراءكم» is an adverb attached to «ارجعوا»; and it has been said: «وراءكم» is an imperative verbal noun (ism fiʿl amr) containing a pronoun as fāʿil. The fāʾ is a conjunction; «التمسوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «ارجعوا»; and «نورًا» is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فضرب بينهم بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله العذاب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ضرب» is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and «بسور» is in the position of a nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; and it has been said: the adverb is the nāʾib fāʿil; and it has been said: the bāʾ is redundant (ṣila) with the nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. «ضرب بينهم سور» (a wall was set up between them). The clause is conjoined to His saying «قيل: ارجعوا». «له» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «باب» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «له باب» is in the position of a genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «سور». «باطنه» is a mubtadaʾ; «فيه» is a fronted khabar, and «الرحمة» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «فيه [الرحمة]» is the khabar of «باطنه»; and the clause is a second ṣifa (adjective) of «سور», or a ṣifa of «باب», and perhaps that is preferable because of its nearness, since a pronoun refers back to the nearest [noun] unless there is a contextual indication (qarīna), and none is determinate here. «وظاهره»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ظاهره» is a mubtadaʾ; «من قبله» is a fronted khabar, and «العذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of «ظاهره», and the whole clause is conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ينادونهم ألم نكن معكم﴾: the clause «ينادونهم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and it has been said: it is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) from the pronoun in the adverb (ẓarf). The hamza is an interrogative particle; «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; «نكن» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «نحن» (we); «معكم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate). The interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an implied [verb of] saying, or it is explicative (tafsīriyya) of the calling, and so has no grammatical position.
﴿قالوا بلى ولكنكم فتنتم أنفسكم وتربصتم وارتبتم﴾: «قالوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «بلى» is a particle of answer that cancels the negation, i.e. yes, you were with us outwardly. «لكن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «كم» is its noun, and the clause «فتنتم أنفسكم» is the khabar of «لكن»; «تربصتم» and «ارتبتم» are conjoined to «فتنتم». What the three verbs relate to is omitted, i.e. you tempted yourselves with hypocrisy, you awaited misfortunes for the believers, and you doubted about the religion.
﴿وغرتكم الأماني حتى جاء أمر الله وغركم بالله الغرور﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, [and «غرتكم الأماني» is] a verb and its fāʿil; «حتى» is a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; «جاء أمر الله» is a verb and its fāʿil; «غركم» is conjoined to «وغرتكم»; «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «غركم»; and «الغرور» is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية ولا من الذين كفروا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of eloquence, pointing to an omitted condition); «اليوم» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يؤخذ»; «لا» is negative; «يؤخذ» is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); «منكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to «يؤخذ»; «فدية» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the verb is masculine because the femininity is figurative; «ولا من الذين كفروا» is conjoined to «منكم»; and the clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿مأواكم النار هي مولاكم وبئس المصير﴾: «مأواكم النار» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), or the reverse; «هي» is a mubtadaʾ, and «مولاكم» is the khabar; «بئس» is an inert (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; «المصير» is the fāʿil (agent); and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being «هي», i.e. the Fire.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿ألم يأن للذين آمنوا أن تخشع قلوبهم لذكر الله وما نزل من الحق﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; «يأن» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. «للذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb], its implied form being «أعني» (I mean), and the preposition and its genitive noun [may also] be attached to «يأن». The clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «أن» with what is in its scope is the fāʿil (agent) of «يأن»; «لذكر الله» is attached to «تخشع»; the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «ذكر الله»; the clause «نزل» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and «من الحق» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ولا يكونوا كالذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبل فطال عليهم الأمد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negative, and «يكونوا» is conjoined to «تخشع»; or «لا» is prohibitive. «يكونوا» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its noun. «كالذين»: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «يكون»; «الذين» is a relative noun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «أوتوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «الكتاب» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من قبل» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أوتوا»; «فطال» is conjoined to «أوتوا»; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «طال»; and «الأمد» is the fāʿil.
﴿فقست قلوبهم وكثير منهم فاسقون﴾: «فقست قلوبهم» is conjoined to «فطال عليهم الأمد»; «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of «كثير», which is why it is permissible to begin with it [as an indefinite mubtadaʾ]; and «فاسقون» is the khabar of «كثير».

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿اعلموا أن الله يحيي الأرض بعد موتها﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «اعلموا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «أن» with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا». «أن» is a particle, the Word of Majesty is its noun, and the clause «يحيي الأرض» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the adverb (ẓarf) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يحيي», and «موتها» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قد بينا لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون﴾: «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «بينا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «بينا»; «الآيات» is the object; «لعل» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing hope (tarajjī), «كم» is its noun, and the clause «تعقلون» is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿إن المصدقين والمصدقات وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعف لهم ولهم أجر كريم﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «المصدقين» is its noun, and «المصدقات» is conjoined to «المصدقين». «أقرضوا» is conjoined to the meaning of the verb in «المصدقين», because the lām [of the article] is in the sense of «الذين» (those who) and the active participle is in the sense of «اصدقوا» (they gave charity), as if it were said: «إن الذين اصدقوا وأقرضوا» (indeed those who gave charity and lent). The Word of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «قرضًا» stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); and «حسنًا» is a naʿt (adjective). «يضاعف» is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of a nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Or the nāʾib fāʿil is a pronoun referring back to the pronoun of giving charity, and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. the reward of giving charity; [in that case] «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضاعف». The wāw is a conjunction; «لهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «أجر» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «كريم» is a naʿt; and the clause «يضاعف لهم» is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنوا», and «رسله» is conjoined to «الله»; «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ, «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and «الصديقون» is the khabar (predicate) of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar is the khabar of the first. Or «هم» is a third mubtadaʾ and «الصديقون» the khabar of «هم», and it with its khabar is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first. The clause «والذين آمنوا...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿والشهداء عند ربهم لهم أجرهم ونورهم﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; or the wāw is resumptive and the clause after it resumptive, with no grammatical position. «الشهداء» is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the adverb (ẓarf) after it, or the clause «لهم أجرهم»; «لهم» is a fronted khabar, «أجرهم» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «نورهم» is conjoined to «أجرهم»; and the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم﴾: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «كذبوا» is conjoined to «كفروا»; «بآياتنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «كفروا»; «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أصحاب الجحيم» is its khabar. [Translator's note: the source attaches «بآياتنا» to «كفروا», although it directly follows «كذبوا»; translated as written.]

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «اعلموا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «أن» with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا»; «أنما» here is [a combination of] a restraining [particle] and a restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). «الحياة» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الدنيا» is a naʿt (adjective) of it; «لعب» is the khabar (predicate) of «الحياة», and what comes after it is coordinated with it; «بينكم» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of «تفاخر»; «في الأموال» is a naʿt of «تكاثر», and «الأولاد» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأموال».
﴿كمثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يكون حطاما﴾: «كمثل»: the kāf is a noun in the sense of «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the meaning of what precedes, i.e. this description is established for it, likened to rain; «مثل» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «أعجب» is a naʿt of «غيث»; «الكفار» is the object of «أعجب», placed first, and they are the tillers; «نباته» is the fāʿil, placed after. «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يهيج» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil is «هو» (it), referring back to the vegetation; «فتراه» is conjoined to «يهيج», the fāʿil of «تراه» is «أنت» (you), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «مصفرًّا» is a ḥāl; and «ثم يكون حطامًا» is conjoined to what precedes.
﴿وفي الآخرة عذاب شديد ومغفرة من الله ورضوان﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «في الآخرة» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; «عذاب» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «شديد» is a naʿt of «عذاب»; «مغفرة» is conjoined to «عذاب»; «من الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣifa of «مغفرة»; and «رضوان» is conjoined to «مغفرة».
﴿وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «الحياة» is the mubtadaʾ, and «الدنيا» is a naʿt of «الحياة»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and «الغرور» is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source does not state the role of «متاع»; it is the khabar of «الحياة».]

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿سابقوا إلى مغفرة من ربكم﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position. «سابقوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «إلى مغفرة» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سابقوا»; and «من ربكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «مغفرة».
﴿وجنة عرضها كعرض السماء والأرض أعدت للذين آمنوا بالله ورسله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «جنة» is conjoined to «مغفرة»; «عرضها» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «كعرض» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), and the clause is a naʿt of «جنة»; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السماوات» [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah has «السماء»]. «أعدت» is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هي» (it); the clause is a second naʿt of «جنة», or resumptive, with no grammatical position. «للذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أعدت»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «بالله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «آمنوا»; and «رسله» is conjoined to «بالله».
﴿ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله ذو الفضل العظيم﴾: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, and «فضل الله» is its khabar; the clause «يؤتيه» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); «يؤتيه» is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من» is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the second object; and the clause «يشاء» is the ṣila of «من», with no grammatical position. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, and «ذو الفضل العظيم» is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ما أصاب من مصيبة في الأرض ولا في أنفسكم إلا في كتاب من قبل أن نبرأها﴾: «ما» is negative; «أصاب» is a past verb; «من مصيبة»: «من» is a redundant (ṣila) preposition, and «مصيبة» is genitive (majrūr) in wording and nominative (marfūʿ) in position, as the fāʿil (agent) of «أصاب». «في الأرض» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مصيبة», or a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أصاب», or to «مصيبة» itself; «ولا في أنفسكم» is conjoined to «في الأرض»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). «في كتاب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مصيبة», because it is specified by the description, or by governing [another word] if «في الأرض» is attached to it; or [it is attached] to an omitted [word], its implied form being «إلا هي كائنة في كتاب» (except that it is [recorded] in a Book), so it is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). «من قبل» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what His saying «في كتاب» is attached to. «نبرأها» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن»; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah the Exalted; and «ها» is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), referring back to the calamity, and it has been said: to the souls, and it has been said: to the earth. «أن» with what is in its scope is in the position of a genitive because the adverb (ẓarf) is annexed to it, and the clause is in the position of a genitive as a ṣifa (adjective) of «كتاب»; and the pronoun in «نبرأها» refers back to the calamity, or to the souls, or to the earth, or to all of that.
﴿إن ذلك على الله يسير﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «ذلك» is its noun; «على الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يسير»; and «يسير» is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿لكيلا تأسوا على ما فاتكم ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم﴾: the lām is a preposition; «كي» is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; «لا» is negative; «تأسوا» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «كي», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «كي» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb], its implied form being «وأعلمناكم» (and We informed you) or «أخبرناكم» (We told you); some implied it as «اختبرناكم» (We tested you). «على ما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تأسوا»; «فاتكم» is a past verb, the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «فاتكم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The wāw is a conjunction, «لا» is negative, and «تفرحوا» is conjoined to «تحزنوا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the ayah is «تأسوا»]; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تفرحوا»; and the clause «آتاكم» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. What «فاتكم» and «آتاكم» relate to is omitted, its implied form being «من النعم» (of blessings).
﴿والله لا يحب كل مختال فخور﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «الله» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «لا يحب» is the khabar (predicate); «كل مختال» is the mafʿūl bihi, and «فخور» is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause «والله لا يحب...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿الذين يبخلون ويأمرون الناس بالبخل﴾: «الذين» is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute) of His saying «كل مختال فخور»; or its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being «فإنهم يستحقون العذاب» (for they deserve punishment); or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم الذين» (they are those who); or it is accusative as blame (ʿalā al-dhamm) by an omitted verb, its implied form being «أذم» (I blame). The clause «يبخلون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «يأمرون» is conjoined to «يبخلون»; «الناس» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «بالبخل» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يأمرون».
﴿ومن يتول فإن الله هو الغني الحميد﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «من» is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; «يتول» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a nominal clause; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Word of Majesty is its noun, «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), «الغني» is the khabar of «إن», and «الحميد» is a second khabar; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the clause «ومن يتول...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿لقد أرسلنا رسلنا بالبينات﴾: the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «أرسلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «رسلنا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «بالبينات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وأنزلنا معهم الكتاب والميزان ليقوم الناس بالقسط﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أنزلنا» is conjoined to «أرسلنا»; «معهم» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl; «الكتاب» is the mafʿūl bihi, and «الميزان» is conjoined to «الكتاب». The lām is causal (taʿlīl); «يقوم» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أرسلنا وأنزلنا»; «بالقسط» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. acting justly and equitably, or to «يقوم».
﴿وأنزلنا الحديد فيه بأس شديد ومنافع للناس﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أنزلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «الحديد» is the mafʿūl bihi; «فيه» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «بأس» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being circumstantial (ḥāliyya) from «الحديد»; «شديد» is a ṣifa (adjective); and «منافع للناس» is conjoined to «بأس شديد».
﴿وليعلم الله من ينصره ورسله بالغيب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «وليعلم» is conjoined to an omitted [element] indicated by the clause «فيه بأس شديد»; the interpreted maṣdar made of «أن يعلم» is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أنزلنا الحديد», and it is conjoined to an implied maṣdar, i.e. «ليستعملوه وليعلم» (so that they may use it, and so that He may know). «الله» is the fāʿil; «مَن» is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi; «ينصر» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هو» (he), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; «رسله» is conjoined to the object of «ينصره», accusative, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and «بالغيب» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the object of «ينصره».
﴿إن الله قوي عزيز﴾: «إن» is for emphasis and the accusative, and the Word of Majesty is its noun; «قوي» is the khabar of «إن», nominative, and «عزيز» is a second khabar, nominative.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ولقد أرسلنا نوحا وإبراهيم وجعلنا في ذريتهما النبوة والكتاب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «أرسلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «نوحًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «إبراهيم» is conjoined to «نوحًا»; «جعلنا» is conjoined to «أرسلنا»; «في ذريتهما» is in the place of the second object; «النبوة» is the first object of «جعلنا»; and «الكتاب» is conjoined to «النبوة».
﴿فمنهم مهتد وكثير منهم فاسقون﴾: the fāʾ is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya); «منهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «مهتد» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كثير», and «فاسقون» is the khabar of «كثير».

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿ثم قفينا على آثارهم برسلنا وقفينا بعيسى ابن مريم وآتيناه الإنجيل﴾: «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «قفينا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «على آثارهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قفينا»; «برسلنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «قفينا»; the clause «قفينا» is conjoined to the clause «جعلنا في ذريتهما»; «بعيسى» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second «قفينا»; «ابن» is a badal (substitute) of «عيسى» or a ṣifa (adjective) of it, and «مريم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «وآتيناه»: the wāw is a conjunction; «آتيناه» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «الإنجيل» is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وجعلنا في قلوب الذين اتبعوه رأفة ورحمة ورهبانية ابتدعوها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «جعلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «في قلوب» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second object of «جعلنا»; «الذين» is muḍāf ilayhi; «اتبعوه» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; «رأفة» is the mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); «ورحمة ورهبانية» are conjoined to «رأفة», accusative; «ابتدعوها» is a past verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and «ها» is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause «ابتدعوها» is a ṣifa of «رهبانية». Or «رهبانية» is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative by an implied (muqaddar) verb indicated by «ابتدعوها», and is not conjoined to what precedes it, because this monasticism was not something Allah prescribed for them, so it is not sound for it to be an object of «جعلنا»; and because monasticism is an action not connected with hearts, while the verb «جعلنا» is restricted by «في قلوب الذين اتبعوه», so its objects are restricted by that. The implied form is «وابتدعوا رهبانية ابتدعوها» (and they invented monasticism — they invented it), and the clause «ابتدعوها» is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله فما رعوها حق رعايتها﴾: «ما» is negative; «كتبناها» is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil, and «ها» is the mafʿūl bihi; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «كتبناها»; the clause «ما كتبناها عليهم» is a ṣifa of «رهبانية», or resumptive, with no grammatical position. «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «ابتغاء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative; «رضوان» is muḍāf ilayhi, and the Word of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi. «فما»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «ما» is negative; «رعوها» is a past verb, indeclinable on a ḍamma implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil, and «ها» is the mafʿūl bihi; «حق» stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; and «رعايتها» is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فآتينا الذين آمنوا منهم أجرهم﴾: «فآتينا»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «آتينا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «الذين» is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi; «آمنوا» is a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «آمنوا»; «أجرهم» is the second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وكثير منهم فاسقون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثير»; «فاسقون» is the khabar (predicate), nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause «وكثير منهم فاسقون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وآمنوا برسوله يؤتكم كفلين من رحمته﴾: «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is a vocative, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and «ها» is for alerting (tanbīh); «الذين» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «أي»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; «اتقوا الله» is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Word of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «آمنوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «اتقوا»; «برسوله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنوا»; «يؤتكم» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi, «كفلين» is the second mafʿūl bihi, and «من رحمته» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كفلين».
﴿ويجعل لكم نورا تمشون به﴾: conjoined to «يؤتكم»; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يجعل», or in the place of the second object; «نورًا» is the object of «يجعل»; and the clause «تمشون به» is a naʿt of «نورًا».
﴿ويغفر لكم والله غفور رحيم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يغفر»; «الله» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «غفور» is a first khabar (predicate), and «رحيم» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ألا يقدرون على شيء من فضل الله﴾: the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); «أن» is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; «لا» is redundant (ṣila); «يعلم» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن»; «أهل الكتاب» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يعلم». «أن» is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»] (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); «لا» is negative; the clause «يقدرون» is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened «أن»; «على شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقدرون»; «من فضل الله» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء»; and «أن» with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of «يعلم».
﴿وأن الفضل بيد الله يؤتيه من يشاء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «أن» with what is in its scope is conjoined to «أن لا يقدرون», falling within the scope of what is known. «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «الفضل» is its noun, and «بيد الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of «أن»; the clause «يؤتيه...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or a second khabar of «أن»; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «من» is the second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause «يشاء» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿والله ذو الفضل العظيم﴾: «الله» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «ذو الفضل» is its khabar, and «العظيم» is a naʿt of «الفضل».

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ i.e. with proofs and arguments. وَأَنْزَلْنا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتابَ i.e. with the rulings and laws. وَالْمِيزانَ: Ibn Zayd said: it is the balance with which people deal with one another; and Qatāda said: the balance is the truth. لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ: accusative (manṣūb) by the lām of purpose (lām kay), and in reality it stands in place of «أن». وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ i.e. for people. فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ: Ibn Zayd said: the mighty harm (al-baʾs al-shadīd) is weapons and swords with which people fight; he said: and the benefits are what lands and mountains are dug with. وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun in يَنْصُرُهُ]. بِالْغَيْبِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ i.e. Strong in taking vengeance on whoever openly confronts Him with enmity, Mighty in His retribution upon him, because no preventer prevents Him from him.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً وَإِبْراهِيمَ to their peoples. وَجَعَلْنا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتابَ فَمِنْهُمْ مُهْتَدٍ i.e. one following the way of guidance, discerning. وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ i.e. going out into disbelief and acts of disobedience.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِرُسُلِنا i.e. We made [them] follow. The pronoun may refer back to the progeny (al-dhurriyya), or to Noah and Abraham, peace be upon them both, because two is a plural. وَقَفَّيْنا بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ i.e. We made [him] follow.
وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ: it is narrated that it was sent down all at once. وَجَعَلْنا فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً: one also says رأفة, and [the verb is] رؤف and رأف. وَرَهْبانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوها: رهبانية is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, i.e. "and they innovated a monasticism", i.e. they originated it; and it is said: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first. ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ: Ibn Zayd said: i.e. We did not make it obligatory. إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ: accusative as an exception that is not of the [kind of the] first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); and it may be a badal (substitute) for the implied pronoun, i.e. "We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the good pleasure of Allah". فَما رَعَوْها حَقَّ رِعايَتِها: its wording is general but what is meant by it is specific; we know of no disagreement about that, and what shows its correctness is فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ. Concerning those who did not observe it there are two views. The position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda is that they are the very ones who innovated it: some of them became Jews and [some] became Christians; and this is narrated from Abū Umāma. As for what is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, they came after those who had innovated it, being disbelievers who took up monasticism and said:
"We follow those who were before us." What shows the correctness of this is the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet ﷺ: فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ — he said: "Whoever believed in me." وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ — he said: "Whoever denied me."

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: of the People of the Book. اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ i.e. in abandoning acts of disobedience to Him and performing His obligations. وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ meaning Muḥammad ﷺ. يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ meaning two portions, as Abū Burda narrated from his father from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Three will be given their reward twice: one who was of the People of the Book and believed in the Torah and the Gospel, then believed in the Qurʾān; a man who had a slave-girl whom he educated and educated her well, then married her; and a slave who was sincere to his master and fulfilled what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made obligatory upon him." وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ: from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the Qurʾān and following the Prophet ﷺ; and Mujāhid said:
guidance. Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj] said: and it is said that it is the light which the believers will have on the Day of Resurrection. وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ i.e. He pardons you and covers your sins for you. وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: possessor of forgiveness and mercy, who does not punish whoever repents.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
لا is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and what comes before and after the passage shows this, i.e. "so that [the People of the Book] may know". It is narrated that Ibn ʿAbbās read لأن يعلم أهل الكتاب, and likewise it is narrated from ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī; and from Ibn Masʿūd لكي يعلم أهل الكتاب, and likewise from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr. These are readings by way of explanation (tafsīr). لا يقدرون: the verb is nominative (raised) because the meaning is "that they are not able" (أنه لا يقدرون); what shows this is that after it comes وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ. Some of the Kufans say that «لا» has the meaning of «ليس»; the first is the view of Sībawayh. Al-Muʿtamir narrated from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Read with the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: ألّا يقدروا without the nūn"; this is on the basis that it is accusative by أن. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is far-fetched in Arabic, that أَنَّ should occur with governing effect after يَعْلَمَ, and it is among the anomalous (shādhdh) [readings]. And among the anomalous [readings] is that it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he read لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ with the nominative [Translator's note: presumably referring to يقدرون, as the source text stands]; its justification is what we mentioned, that the implied form in it is "that they [are not able]" and "that the bounty is in the hand of Allah", i.e. in the hand of Allah and not theirs, because, as is narrated, they said: "The prophets are from among us", and so they disbelieved in ʿĪsā ﷺ and in Muḥammad; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that the bounty is in His hand: He sends whom He wills and bestows favour on whom He wishes. Except that Qatāda said:
When Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ, the Jews envied the Muslims, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ أَلَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى شَيْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ i.e. of His creation. وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ i.e. towards His servants.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
سَبَّحَ: He magnified and exalted; it is derived from السباحة, which is rising. The implied form is: ما في السّموات وما في الأرض ("what is in the heavens and what is in the earth"); «ما» [the second one] was omitted, according to the position of Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad], and it is indefinite, not a relative noun, because a relative noun is not omitted. The grammarians recited: [rajaz metre] 463-
لو قلت ما في قومها لم تيثم ... يفصلها في حسب وميسم
(If you said "There is none among her people…", you would not commit a sin, "…who surpasses her in lineage and beauty.")
So the implied form is: من يفضلها ("one who surpasses her") [Translator's note: the verse has «يفصلها» in the printed text, the gloss «يفضلها»]. وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e. the Mighty in His vengeance on whoever disobeys Him, the One against whom none of His enemies whom He punishes can gain victory; the Wise in His management of His creation, the One into whose management no defect enters.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and nominative because it is an imperfect verb. وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ: likewise. No verb has been pronounced from الأول, though it is on [the pattern] afʿal, because its fāʾ and ʿayn [first and second radicals] are from one place, so that was felt to be heavy. الآخر does not run parallel to a verb [i.e. it is not the active participle of its verb], because it is from تأخّر.
وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ: It was said: the meaning of الظاهر is the One whose making and wisdom are manifest. It was also said: the One who knows what is manifest and what is hidden. Among the best of what has been said about it is that it is from ظهر, i.e. became strong and high; so the meaning is: the One who prevails over everything, who is high above it, so things are beneath Him. الباطن: [He is within] all things, so nothing is nearer to anything than He; and like it is وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ [Qāf: 16]. What indicates this is that after it comes وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ, i.e. nothing is hidden from Him.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: الَّذِي may be in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), because it is at the beginning of a verse. He said: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of what preceded, and it may be in the position of the accusative as praise: "I mean by this praise the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself on the Throne." يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنْها وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها: One says ولج يلج when something enters. The origin is يولج; the wāw was dropped because it is between a yāʾ and a kasra. وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is the meaning, i.e. He is a witness with you wherever you are. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ: i.e. of the good and the bad, the obedience and the disobedience that you do, so that He may recompense you for it.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: i.e. authority over them both, so His command and His ruling are effective in them. وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ: i.e. to Him is your destination, so that He may recompense you for your deeds.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ: i.e. [He makes] the decrease of the night [enter] into the day, so that there is an increase [in it]. وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ: He makes the decrease of the day enter into the night, so that there is an increase in it — as ʿIkrima and Ibrāhīm [al-Nakhaʿī] said: this is about shortening and lengthening. The wāw was not dropped from يولج, although it is between a yāʾ and a kasra, because the verb is quadriliteral [i.e. of form IV, أولج], and it is not permissible to change it with this change. وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ: i.e. of the good and the bad that you conceal in your breasts, or that you intend in yourselves. In the ḥadīth: "Supplication is answered after reciting these six verses."

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: i.e. they succeed those who were before them. He urged them to spend because they will perish as those before them perished, and [what they have] will be inherited. فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْفَقُوا: الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. those of you who believe in Allah and His Messenger. لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ: i.e. a great reward.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t:
وَما لَكُمْ لا تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ: [لا تؤمنون is] in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: what is the matter with you, if you are abandoning faith? وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ: having made the proofs and arguments manifest. لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ: al-Farrāʾ said: all the readers read وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ; he said: and had it been read وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ it would have been correct. [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing the two forms has been lost in the printed text; they are أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُم (active, "He has taken your covenant") and أُخِذَ مِيثاقُكُم (passive, "your covenant has been taken"), the latter being Abū ʿAmr's reading.] Abū Jaʿfar said: These are his exact words in his book, and it is an error, for Abū ʿAmr read وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ [i.e. the passive]. However, Abū ʿUbayd said: the reading in our view is the first, وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ, because the community (al-umma) holds to it, and because the mention of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, [comes] before the verse and after it. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for his saying "because the community holds to it," it is a clear proof, because the umma is the multitude. As for his saying "because the mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic be His name, [comes] before the verse and after it," it does not follow, because the meaning is known.

The scholars have two views on the taking of the covenant. One of them is that He took the covenant when they were brought out from the back of Ādam ﷺ, [that they would affirm] that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is their Lord, and that they have no god other than Him; this is the position of the scholars among the people of ḥadīth, among them Mujāhid. The other view is that it is figurative: since the signs of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, are clear, the indications plain and His wisdom manifest, to which whoever sees them testifies, his knowledge of that is equivalent to a covenant being taken from him. إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ: It was said: the meaning is: if you are resolved upon faith, this is its time, because of the proofs and indications that have become manifest to you. What indicates this is that after it comes هو الذي ينزّل على عبده آيات بيّنات. لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ: i.e. from the darkness of unbelief to the light of faith; as Mujāhid said: from misguidance to guidance.
وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ: i.e. when He made clear to you your guidance.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
وَما لَكُمْ أَلَّا تُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative according to the meaning: "and what excuse do you have for not spending in the way of Allah?" وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: By this He urged them to spend, because they will die and leave behind what they were stingy with, and it will be inherited from them. لا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ وَقاتَلَ: The scholars differed about the meaning of this conquest (al-fatḥ). Qatāda said: those of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who spent before the conquest of Mecca and fought are more excellent than those who spent after the conquest of Mecca and fought; and Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise. al-Shaʿbī said: those who spent before al-Ḥudaybiya and fought are of a higher rank than those who spent after the conquest of al-Ḥudaybiya and fought.

Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is more likely to be correct, because ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār related from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī; he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us on the day of the conquest of al-Ḥudaybiya: "Peoples will come whose deeds will make you think little of your own deeds compared with theirs." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they from Quraysh?" He said: "No, they are the people of Yemen, the most tender of heart and the gentlest of soul." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they better than us?" He said: "No. If one of them had a mountain of gold and then spent it, it would not reach a mudd of one of you, nor half of it. This is the difference between us and [other] people." [Translator's note: the printed text has «بعيننا», apparently for «بيننا».] لا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ وَقاتَلَ أُولئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَقاتَلُوا وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ.

Abū Ḥātim reported «وكلّ وعد الله الحسنى» in the nominative. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh permitted the like of this by implying the hāʾ [i.e. وعده], and recited: [mutaqārib metre] 464-
فثوب نسيت وثوب أجرّ
(So a garment I forgot, and a garment I trail.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd does not permit this in prose or verse, unless something other than what Sībawayh assumed is possible in it, namely that the verb is a naʿt (adjective), the implied form being "for there is a garment [that] I forgot"; on this basis only the nominative is permissible in ثوب. He does not permit زيد ضربت, because there is nothing of this in it. So كلّ would mean "and those are all [ones whom] Allah has promised," [the verb] being a naʿt. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e. of spending and stinginess, so that He may recompense you for it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
مَنْ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), ذَا is its khabar (predicate), and الَّذِي is a naʿt (adjective) of ذا. There are two other views on it. One of them is that «ذا» is redundant (zāʾida) together with الذي. The other view is that «ذا» is redundant together with «من»; this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, and he claimed that he saw in one of the copies of the Muṣḥaf of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] «منذا», with the nūn joined to the dhāl, the two being made one thing. The Basrans do not permit «ذا» to be redundant with «من», but permit that with «ما», because «ما» is vague (mubhama), so ذا is of the same kind as it. On this basis was read وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ قُلِ الْعَفْوَ [al-Baqara: 219] in the accusative. Making «ذا» redundant with «الذي» is more likely: do you not see that «الذي» is made diminutive as «ذا» is made diminutive, so one says اللّذيّا, and one says ذيّا?

Sībawayh was challenged on his saying that الذي is equivalent to العمي; it was said: how can this be? For one says in the diminutive of العمي: العميّ, and one says in the diminutive of الذي: اللذيّا, and one says اللّذيان and العميان, so all of this is taken as different; so how can الذي be equivalent to العمي? Nothing follows from this, and this is not the place to explain it.

«قرضا» is accusative as being a noun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as one says أجابه إجابة, and it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as you say أقرضته مالا ("I lent him money"). «حسنا» is a naʿt of قرض. It was said: the meaning of الحسن here is the lawful, for lending [to Allah] is spending in hope of reward from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, seeking what is with Him. فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ: al-Farrāʾ said: he made it conjoined to يقرض, as you say "Who will come, and honour me, and do good to me?" Abū Isḥāq said: it may be cut off from the first, resumptive. Whoever reads فيضعفه [Translator's note: with the accusative, فيضعِّفَه/فيضاعفَه] makes it the answer to the interrogative and puts it in the accusative by an implied «أن», according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, while al-Jarmī puts it in the accusative by the fāʾ. وَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ: It was said: the Garden.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
You put يوما in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. they have a reward on that day. «ترى» is in the position of the genitive by the iḍāfa (genitive construct). «يسعى» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). As for His saying, Majestic and Mighty, بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ, without mentioning the left sides, the scholars have three views on it. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: their light is their guidance; and Muḥammad ibn Jarīr inclined to this view. He said: because the believers' light is around them on every side, so when Allah, Majestic and Mighty, specified "before them and on their right," it was known that it is not illumination; and the bāʾ has the meaning of «في». One of the Basran grammarians said: it has the meaning of عن. Abū Jaʿfar said: It was also said: the light here is the light of their books, and they are only given their books in their right hands, from in front of them; for this reason the specification occurred. Abū Jaʿfar said: The most excellent thing said about this is what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah have mercy on him, said; he said: the believers are given lights according to their deeds; among them is one who is given a light like a mountain, and the least of that is that one is given a light on his big toe [or thumb] which shines at one time and goes out at another.

بُشْراكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: i.e. it is said to them — the "saying" being omitted. «بشراكم» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «جنات» is its khabar (predicate). al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative in «جنّات» in two ways: one of them by "cutting off" (qaṭʿ), with اليوم in the position of the khabar although it is an adverb; and he permitted the nominative of «اليوم» as the khabar of «بشراكم». And he permitted «بشراكم» to be in the position of the accusative, meaning "they give them good tidings with the good tidings," and «جنات» to be put in the accusative by «البشرى».

Abū Jaʿfar said: We know of no one among the grammarians who mentioned this except him, and it is strained, because جَنَّاتٌ, if he put it in the accusative by cutting off, is not in the sense of a verb after that; and if he put it in the accusative by البشرى — if he put it in the accusative by بشراكم, it is a clear error, because it would be included in the ṣila (relative clause), so the ṣila would be separated from the relative [i.e. the maṣdar] by اليوم, which is not in the ṣila, and this is not permissible according to any of the grammarians. And if «جنات» is put in the accusative by an omitted verb, it is something strained; moreover, no one has read it so. خالِدِينَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ: al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [it is] ذلك الفوز العظيم, without «هو». Abū Jaʿfar said: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, and «هو» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ is the khabar of ذلك. It is also possible for «هو» to be a second mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of ذلك.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
You put يوما in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "and that is the great triumph on that day"; it may also be a badal (substitute) for the يوم before it. انْظُرُونا is from نظر ينظر in the sense of looking (al-naẓar), and this is the clear reading.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read وأنظرونا with fatḥa on the hamza [i.e. أَنظِرونا]. Abū Ḥātim claimed that this is an error; he said: this only comes to us from the direction of Kufa. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the one who judged Ḥamza to have erred in this only did so because he took «أنظرنا» to mean "defer us and give us respite," which is not permissible here. In my view it can bear something else, because one says أنظرني in the sense of "take your time with me and be gentle," and on this the meaning is sound. نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ: jussive (majzūm) because it is an apodosis (jawāb). قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَراءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُوراً: i.e. the believers said to the hypocrites: go back to the place where we were and seek the light there.

Abū Jaʿfar said: The explanation of this is what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: Darkness will cover the people — the believers, the hypocrites and the unbelievers — then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will send a light by which the believers are guided to the Garden. When the believers follow it, the hypocrites follow them, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, will set up between them a wall, within which is mercy and outside of which, facing it, is punishment. The hypocrites will call out to the believers: انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ, and the believers will say to them: ارْجِعُوا وَراءَكُمْ — to the place where we were, in which there was darkness and then the light came — and seek the light from it.

Abū Jaʿfar said: فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِسُورٍ: [بسور] is in the position of the nominative as the noun whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); according to the view of Muḥammad ibn Yazīd it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by the verb. The ḍād in «ضرب» was given ḍamma to make a distinction. If it is said: why was it not given kasra? The answer according to some grammarians is that it was given ḍamma just as the beginning of a noun is given ḍamma in the diminutive. This answer needs two answers: one of them is the answer to why the beginning of the diminutive noun is given ḍamma, [and the other,] why the beginning of the passive verb is given ḍamma. The answer is that the beginning of the passive verb was given ḍamma because, when a distinction between it and the active verb was necessary, it could not be given kasra except for another reason, because the active verb itself sometimes comes with kasra in the speech of some of them — أنت تِعلم and نحن نِستعين — and it comes with fatḥa, which is the regular pattern; so nothing remained but the ḍamma. This is not the place for the answer about the diminutive. [Translator's note: the printed text has «بينه ما سمّي فاعله», apparently for «بنية ما سمّي فاعله», "the form of the active verb".]

لَهُ بابٌ: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: the Gate of Mercy which is in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) is the one Allah, Majestic and Mighty, mentioned. Qatāda said: باطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ: the Garden and what is in it; وَظاهِرُهُ مِنْ قِبَلِهِ الْعَذابُ: the Fire.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
يُنادُونَهُمْ أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ: i.e. we prayed with you, fasted, inherited from you and intermarried with you. قالُوا بَلى: i.e. you were indeed with us like that. وَلكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ: Mujāhid said: by hypocrisy. وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ: Ibn Zayd said: [you waited] with faith [i.e. delayed it]. وَارْتَبْتُمْ: he said: they doubted. Someone else said: ارتبتم means you acted as those who doubt the promise and threat of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمانِيُّ: i.e. your own wishful fancies deceived you, so you turned away from the way of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. حَتَّى جاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: It was said: His decree of your deaths. وَغَرَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ: Mujāhid and Qatāda said: الغرور is Satan. Abū Jaʿfar said: faʿūl in the speech of the Arabs is for intensiveness, and according to the Basrans it is transitive. You say: هذه غرور زيدا ("this one is a great deceiver of Zayd") and غفور الذنب ("much-forgiving of the sin"). Sībawayh recited, regarding its taking an object: [ramal metre] 465-
ثمّ زادوا أنّهم في قومهم ... غفر ذنبهم غير فجر
(Then they surpassed [others] in that among their people they are forgiving of their sin, not wicked.)

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ: Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read تؤخذ with tāʾ because الفدية is feminine; whoever made it masculine did so because it and الفداء are one [in meaning], and it is the substitute and compensation. وَلا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: i.e. no substitute or compensation will be taken from those who disbelieved in place of their punishment. مَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ: i.e. your dwelling is the Fire; a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Likewise هِيَ مَوْلاكُمْ. وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ: i.e. and wretched is the destination, the Fire; then this was omitted.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
And from al-Ḥasan: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ [Translator's note: the variant attributed to al-Ḥasan is not distinguishable in the printed text; the beginning of the entry appears to be missing]. One says أإن يئين [Translator's note: so in the printed text, presumably آن يئين], أنى يأنى and حان يحين, and نال ينال and أنال ينيل, with one meaning. «أن» is in the position of the nominative by يأن. وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ: «ما» is in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and for what has come down"; this is the reading of Shayba and Nāfiʿ. Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and the Kufans read وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ [Translator's note: with doubling, i.e. نزّل, as the following discussion shows; the shadda has been lost in the printed text]. It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read وما أنزل من الحقّ. Abū ʿUbayd chooses the doubled form because the mention of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, precedes it. Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is the same, because the truth does not come down until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends it down, and there is no room for choice in this; and if it were permissible to speak of choice in the like of this, it would be said: the choice is نزل, because before it comes لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ, and He did not say "for Allah's reminding" (لتذكير الله).

وَلا يَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلُ: يكونوا is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «تخشع», i.e. "and that they not be"; it may also be in the position of the jussive (majzūm). The first is preferable, because it is a conjunctive wāw, and what follows it is not cut off from what precedes it except with evidence. فَطالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَمَدُ: Mujāhid said: time (al-dahr). فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ: i.e. they did not soften and did not accept admonition. وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). They were not all described as sinful, because among them are those who believed, and among them are those whom the call did not reach and who remain upon what their prophet ﷺ brought.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها: It was said: the One who did this is the One who guides and sets aright whomever He wills to guide, including whoever has strayed from the path of truth. قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ: i.e. with the arguments and proofs, so that you may be in hope of understanding that. This is the view of Sībawayh. Someone else says: «لعلّ» has the meaning of «كي» (so that); but if it were so, it would have been تعقلوا without the nūn.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَالْمُصَّدِّقاتِ: The origin is المتصدقين, then the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād. In the reading of Ubayy it is إنّ المتصدقين, and in the reading of Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ [Translator's note: i.e. المُصَدِّقين with an undoubled ṣād; the vowelling has been lost in the printed text], i.e. the believers, from التصديق (affirming as true), while the first is from الصدقة (charity). وَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ: It was said: the Garden.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject). أُولئِكَ may be a second mubtadaʾ, and it may be a badal (substitute) for الذين. It cannot be a naʿt (adjective), because a vague noun (mubham, i.e. demonstrative) cannot be a naʿt of what has the alif and lām; مررت بالرجل هذا is not permissible as naʿt according to anyone I know of, whereas if you said مررت بزيد هذا as naʿt it would be permissible. The khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the printed text has «وخير», for «وخبر»] is الصِّدِّيقُونَ. Abū Isḥāq said: صدّيق is for intensiveness, i.e. one who affirms the truth a great deal. Someone else said: this is an error, because fiʿʿīl only comes from the triliteral, like سكّيت from سكت; and صدّيق is for one who is truthful a great deal. From this Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was called al-Ṣiddīq, so that he was known by it in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, named Abū Bakr ṣiddīq."

وَالشُّهَداءُ: on this view they are conjoined to الصدّيقين. What indicates the soundness of that is what Ibn ʿAjlān related from Zayd ibn Aṣamm from al-Barāʾ from the Prophet ﷺ; he said: "The believers of my community are martyrs," then he recited: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيقُونَ وَالشُّهَداءُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ — the verse. Abū Jaʿfar said: So this view is preferable from the standpoint of ḥadīth and of Arabic, because the wāw is a conjunctive wāw, so what follows it is to be included in what precedes it, unless something prevents that, namely a decisive proof.

It was also said: the [sense is] complete at أولئك هم الصديقون, and الشهداء is a new beginning (mubtadaʾ). This is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is the choice of Muḥammad ibn Jarīr, who claimed it is more likely to be correct, because the known meaning of الشهداء is the one killed in the way of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Then he made an exception and said: unless what is meant by الشهداء is that he testifies for himself before his Lord to faith. Abū Jaʿfar said: If «والشهداء» is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar is عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ; or its khabar may be لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ, and this is conjoining a clause to a clause. The first [view] is otherwise: «والشهداء» is conjoined to الصدّيقين, and لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ is for all of them. وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا: a mubtadaʾ.
أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, in the position of the khabar of the first.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ: «ما» restrains (kāffa) أنّ from governing; had you made it a relative [lit. ṣila] you would have put الحياة in the accusative. الدنيا is [part] of its naʿt (adjective). لَعِبٌ is the khabar (predicate). The meaning is "like play," i.e. a person rejoices in his life in it as he rejoices in play, then his life passes away as his play passes away — and its adornment, and the abundance of wealth and children with which people boast and vie with one another. كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَباتُهُ: Abū Isḥāq said: the kāf is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt, i.e. "and boasting like rain." He said: it may also be a khabar after a khabar. الكفّار are the tillers [lit. those who cover the seed]; and when something pleases the tillers it is at the utmost of beauty. He said: they may also be the unbelievers themselves, because the world pleases the unbelievers more intensely, since they do not believe in the resurrection. He said: «يهيج» means it begins to turn yellow. ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطاماً: he said: broken into pieces. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, struck this as a parable for the life of this world and its passing away. Then He, Majestic and Mighty, informed of what is in the Hereafter and said: وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٌ وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr said, from Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ; he said:
"The space of a whip in the Garden is better than the world and what is in it. Recite, if you wish: وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ."

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
سابِقُوا إِلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ: i.e. race, by the deeds that bring about forgiveness, to forgiveness from your Lord. وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها كَعَرْضِ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: A number of scholars have spoken about the meaning of this. Among them are those who said: العرض here is breadth (spaciousness). Among them are those who said: it is like the night and the day — when they go, Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best where they go; ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, gave this answer. Among them are those who said: this is the Garden which the believers will enter on the Day of Resurrection.

السماء is feminine; al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, and other grammarians apart from al-Farrāʾ mentioned that, and the Qur'an came with it: إِذَا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ [al-Inshiqāq: 1] and إِذَا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ [al-Infiṭār: 1]. al-Farrāʾ reported that it is treated as feminine and masculine, and recited: [wāfir metre] 466-
فلو رفع السّماء إليه قوما ... لحقنا بالسّماء مع السّحاب
(If the sky [i.e. He] had raised a people to Himself, we would have joined the sky along with the clouds.)
Even if this verse were a proof, it would be construed otherwise, namely as treating the whole [i.e. a plural] as masculine. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd mentioned that سماء can be the plural of سماوة, and he and others recited: [wāfir metre] 467-
سماوة الهلال حتّى احقوقفا
(Like the shape of the crescent moon, until it curved.)
What indicates the soundness of this is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إِلَى السَّماءِ فَسَوَّاهُنَّ [al-Baqara: 29].

When السماء is singular, its femininity is like the femininity of عناق (she-kid). It is pluralised in six ways: among them two sound plurals, two broken plurals of paucity and two broken plurals of multitude. That is your saying: سموات, سماءات, أسم, أسمية, سمايا and سميّ — and if you wish you can give kasra to the sīn of سميّ. Another [form] has come for it in poetry, as [the poet] said: [ṭawīl metre] 468-
سماء الإله فوق سبع سمائيا
(The heaven of God, above seven heavens.)
So on this basis سماء was pluralised as سماء [i.e. سمائي]. There is more than one difficulty and subtle point of grammar in it. Among them: he likened سماء to رسالة, since the hāʾ in رسالة is augmented, and the measure of فعال and فعالة is one; so on this basis he should have said سمايا. But he did something else: he pluralised it as سماء according to the original form, because the origin of خطايا is خطاء. Then he did a third thing: he should have said فوق سبع سماء, but he treated the defective [root] like the sound one and made it equivalent to the diptote among sound nouns, and added the alif for prolonging the rhyme (iṭlāq).

الأرض is feminine, and masculine treatment of it has been reported, as [the poet] said: [mutaqārib metre] 469-
فلا مزنة ودقت ودقها ... ولا أرض أبقل ابقالها
(No rain-cloud has rained as it rained, and no land has sprouted herbs as it sprouted.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: Some rejected this and transmitted «ولا أرض أبقلت ابقالها» with lightening of the hamza. Ibn Kaysān said: in their saying أرضون they gave this rāʾ a vowel because they intended أرضات, so they built it according to what is required in the plural with alif and tāʾ. He said: and they pluralised it with wāw and nūn as compensation for the dropping of the hāʾ in its singular.

ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e. that bounty — of divine enabling, guidance and reward — is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whomever He wills, i.e. He gives it to whomever He wills of His creation. وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِلاَّ فِي كِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ (22): Qatāda said: فِي الْأَرْضِ means the years [of hardship], i.e. war and drought. وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ: pains and illnesses — but [it is] in a Book. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها: it is "before We create the souls"; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd. It was also said: the pronoun is for the earth; and it was said: for the afflictions. The first is the most appropriate, because the eminent [scholars] held it, and it is nearer to the pronoun. One of the scholars said: this is the meaning of Allah's decree and predestination: that He wrote down everything that will be, so that the angels may know the greatness of His power, Majestic and Mighty. إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ: because He, Majestic and Mighty, only says to a thing "Be," and it is.

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ: i.e. of worldly matters, since Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has informed you that it is settled and written. وَلا تَفْرَحُوا بِما آتاكُمْ: and that is the joy that leads to disobedience. Abū ʿAmr read ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم [Translator's note: i.e. أتاكم without the long ā, "what has come to you", as the following argument shows; the distinction has been lost in the printed text], and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He argued that if it were آتاكم ("He gave you"), the first would be أفاتكم ("He made you miss").

Abū Jaʿfar said: This argument is rejected by the scholars and the people of reasoning, because the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not construed according to analogies; it is only construed according to what the multitude transmits — so if a man comes and applies analogy, [he may do so only] after being a follower [of transmission]. The reading is only taken as we have said, or as Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym said: "I did not read a single letter until two or more of the leading [readers] agreed on it." So the reading of Nāfiʿ came to be from three or more. We know of no one who read this which Abū ʿUbayd chose except Abū ʿAmr. Moreover, what he turned away from has a known and sound meaning: everyone with intelligence and knowledge knows that whatever a person misses or receives, it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who made him miss it or gave it to him — even if this were known only from His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها. والله لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ: i.e. [proud] in his gait out of arrogance and self-importance, boastful towards people of his wealth and his worldly goods; rather, he ought to be humble before Allah, Majestic and Mighty, thank Him and praise Him.

الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ (24) الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ: i.e. with the rights that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has over them. وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ: i.e. with what they themselves do of that. There are five ways of parsing الَّذِينَ: three of them for the nominative and two for the accusative. الَّذِينَ may be in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). It may be in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar (predicate) being omitted, indicated by what is predicated of its counterparts. The third way is that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and what comes after it — the condition and its apodosis — indicates its khabar, because it has its meaning. It may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for كلّ, or in the sense of "I mean" (أعني). وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ: i.e. free of need of His creation and of what they spend, praised by them for His bestowing favours upon them. Whoever reads فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ makes «هو» redundant (zāʾida), carrying the sense of emphasis, or a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as khabar, the clause being the khabar of «إن».

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) a relative noun in the position of the nominative (fī maḥall rafʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "معذّبون" (they will be punished) [Note: It may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", the clause being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) ... just as it may be a badal (substitute) for (كلّ مختال) in the previous verse (23).], (بالبخل) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأمرون). (الواو) a conjunction. (من) a conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الغنيّ, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.].
The clause «الذين يبخلون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يبخلون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «يأمرون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause. The clause «من يتولّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يتولّ ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.]. The clause «إنّ الله ... الغنيّ» is in the position of the jussive (fī maḥall jazm) as the apodosis [Note: The clause may be a causal explanation (taʿlīl) for an omitted apodosis, i.e.: whoever turns away, Allah is free of need of him, because Allah is the Free of need.]

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (بالبيّنات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object or from the agent. (الواو) a conjunction in the following places. (معهم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to a ḥāl from الكتاب, i.e. "carried with them". (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl). (يقوم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām. (بالقسط) attached to (يقوم), by its being made to imply (taḍmīn) the meaning of "يتعاملون" (they deal with one another) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقوم ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزلنا، أرسلنا). (فيه) attached to an advanced khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (بأس). (للناس) attached to (منافع). (ليعلم) like ليقوم. (رسله) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the absent pronoun in (ينصره). (بالغيب) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in ينصره..
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive. The clause «أنزلنا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the oath. The clause «يقوم الناس ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن). The clause «أنزلنا (the second)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أنزلنا (the first). The clause «فيه بأس ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from الحديد. The clause «يعلم الله ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second implied particle-relative (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزلنا الحديد); and it is conjoined to an implied maṣdar, i.e. "ليستعملوه وليعلم ..." (that they may use it and that He may know ...).
The clause «ينصره ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من). The clause «إنّ الله قوي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:26-27.t:
* I'rab:
(ولقد أرسلنا) its i'rab has preceded [Note: In the previous verse (25).]. (الواو) a conjunction in the four places. (في ذرّيتهما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), placed first. (الفاء) for subdivision (tafrīʿ). (منهم) attached to an advanced khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مهتد), which is nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the deleted yāʾ, as it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). And the second (منهم) is a naʿt (adjective) of (كثير).
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive. The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath. The clause «منهم مهتد ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «كثير منهم فاسقون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause منهم مهتد.
27- (على آثارهم) attached to (قفّينا), and likewise (برسلنا). (بعيسى) attached to the second (قفّينا). (في قلوب) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. (رهبانية) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to رأفة by the wāw [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), explained by the mentioned verb, i.e.: ابتدعوا رهبانيّة.]. (ما) negative. (عليهم) attached to (كتبناها). (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr). (ابتغاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb). (الفاء) a conjunction in the two places. (حقّ) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is annexed to the maṣdar. (منهم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of آمنوا, and the second (منهم) is a naʿt of (كثير).
The clause «قفّينا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause جعلنا. The clause «قفّينا (the second)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause قفّينا (the first). The clause «آتيناه ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause قفّينا (the second). The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause آتيناه. The clause «ابتدعوها» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of رهبانية. The clause «ما كتبناها ...» is in the position of the accusative as a second naʿt of رهبانيّة. The clause «رعوها ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كتبناها. The clause «آتينا ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause ما رعوها. The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين). The clause «كثير ... فاسقون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, carrying the meaning of explaining the cause (taʿlīl) of their failure to observe it.

* Morphology:
(27) رهبانيّة: a noun of relation (ism mansūb) to الرهبان (the monks), so it is of the type of the artificial maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-ṣināʿī); or it is originally a maṣdar meaning ascetic discipline, withdrawal from people and becoming a monk; its pattern is فعلانيّة, with fatḥa then sukūn. (رعوها) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is رعاوها: two vowelless letters met, so the alif, the lām (third radical) of the word, was deleted, and it became رعوها, and what precedes the wāw remained with fatḥa as an indication of the deleted alif; its pattern is فعوها ...
(رعايتها) an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb رعي, meaning "to guard and manage affairs"; its pattern is فعالة, with kasra on the fāʾ.
[Translator's note: The source writes the verb as «رعي»; the usual form is رعى.]

* Benefits:
- The single wāw..
It is divided into the following kinds:
1- The conjunctive wāw (al-ʿāṭifa), whose meaning is absolute combination, as in His saying, Exalted is He: فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ, and وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً وَإِبْراهِيمَ.
2- That it be in the meaning of the bāʾ of the genitive, as in their saying: (أنت أعلم ومالك), i.e. بمالك (you know best about your property).
3- The wāw of resumption (al-istiʾnāf), after which the verb is nominative, as in His saying, Exalted is He: لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي الْأَرْحامِ ما نَشاءُ.
